articles.summary: College basketball is finally here. Check out the odds to win the 2026-2027 NCAA Tournament heading into the season.

Can Michigan defend its crown without its coach from a season ago, or will a new champion cut down the nets? But plenty has changed since Michigan cut down the nets. May left to coach the Dallas Mavericks, and the Wolverines’ title odds have lengthened from +600 in April to +4000, outside the top 10 on the oddsboard. New head coach Mike Boynton Jr. inherits a championship backcourt of Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, along with several incoming transfers. Still, Michigan has major holes to fill after losing Yaxel Lendeborg, Morez Johnson Jr. and Aday Mara. Lendeborg is already averaging 22.7 points per game through the first few weeks of his NBA career.

articles.title: “It makes my heart feel good": Tonya Harding makes emotional figure skating comeback at 55 after decades away from the ice
articles.summary: Tonya Harding is preparing to return to the ice, decades after a scandal ended her competitive figure skating career. The former U.S.
articles.body: Tonya Harding is preparing to return to the ice, decades after a scandal ended her competitive figure skating career. The former U.S. champion, now 55, hopes to perform in front of a live audience this December. Her comeback is not about chasing medals or rewriting her past. Instead, Harding wants to reconnect with the sport that shaped much of her life, even as she works to rebuild the strength needed to skate again.Tonya Harding prepares for December skating show with harness trainingTonya Harding discussed her plans in an October 30 interview with KOIN 6, revealing that she will take part in a public skating event called “Tonya and Friends” on December 12. The show will take place at Mountain View Ice Arena in Vancouver, Washington.Harding's return has required patience. Harding began skating twice a week in the spring, hoping that an opportunity to perform would eventually come along. She now uses a harness during practice as she works to improve her balance, stamina and strength.The training offers a glimpse of how much work goes into returning to a physically demanding sport after years away. Harding is not currently eligible to compete in official U.S. Figure Skating Association events, but the December appearance gives her a chance to perform for fans again.“I just want people to come out and have fun and be able to enjoy a real skating show,” she told KOIN 6.She also made clear that her attachment to skating has never faded.“The love of skating is the reason why I’ve always come back,” she told the outlet. “I just can’t walk away from it.”.Her former coach, Dody Teachman, who is helping her prepare for the show, also praised her determination. “She’s a force all her own.”Tonya Harding's skating comeback revisits a controversial pastTonya Harding rose to fame in 1991 after becoming the first American woman to land a triple Axel in competition at the U.S. Championships. She won the national title that year and later earned silver at the World Championships. She also represented the United States at the 1992 Winter Olympics.However, her career took a dramatic turn before the 1994 Winter Olympics. Nancy Kerrigan was attacked with a metal baton, and the investigation exposed a conspiracy involving Harding's former husband, Jeff Gillooly, and her bodyguard, Shawn Eckardt. They had arranged for Shane Stant to assault Kerrigan.Harding denied knowing about the attack beforehand but later pleaded guilty to conspiracy to hinder the investigation. She received probation, community service and a $160,000 fine. The U.S. Figure Skating Association subsequently banned her for life from competing in or coaching the sport.Her life after skating included professional boxing, television appearances and renewed public attention through the 2017 film I, Tonya, starring Margot Robbie. Harding also competed on Dancing with the Stars and won Worst Cooks in America: Celebrity Edition.Now, her December performance offers a different kind of return. Harding says skating still brings her happiness, and she is eager to share that feeling with an audience.“It makes my heart feel good,” Harding said about her return. “And I am really glad people can come see me skate again.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Un desconocido tumba al campeón olímpico de surf y desata la locura en Filipinas
articles.standfirst: Jayuard Alciso, invitado local al Philippines Pro, elimina a Kauli Vaast por apenas 76 centésimas en Cloud 9. El histórico estreno del Championship Tour en el país deja dos victorias filipinas ante la élite mundial.
articles.summary: Jayuard Alciso, invitado local al Philippines Pro, elimina a Kauli Vaast por apenas 76 centésimas en Cloud 9. El histórico estreno del Championship Tour en el país deja dos victorias filipinas ante la élite mundial.
articles.body: El campeón olímpico de París 2024 acaba de sufrir una de las derrotas más inesperadas del circuito mundial. Kauli Vaast, el surfista francés que conquistó el oro en Teahupo'o, cayó este domingo ante Jayuard Alciso, un invitado filipino que competía en casa, en la temida ola de Cloud 9. El resultado, 12,93 frente a 12,17 puntos, decidió una eliminatoria de infarto por apenas 76 centésimas y provocó una celebración multitudinaria en la isla de Siargao, escenario por primera vez de una prueba del Championship Tour. Alciso, que consiguió su plaza mediante el clasificatorio local, firmó una actuación decisiva con dos olas de 7,33 y 5,60 puntos. Pero no fue el único protagonista de la jornada. Su compatriota John Mark Tokong, conocido como el rey de Cloud 9, derrotó al brasileño Samuel Pupo por 16,60 a 11,00, logrando la primera victoria de un filipino en una manga del Championship Tour. Dos resultados que convirtieron el estreno del circuito en Filipinas en una auténtica fiesta nacional. La aventura de ambos locales terminó este lunes 2 de noviembre: Tokong fue eliminado por el australiano Ethan Ewing (14,50-11,54) y Alciso cayó ante el japonés Kanoa Igarashi (12,90-11,84). Sin embargo, sus victorias del domingo ya forman parte de la historia del surf filipino. El Philippines Pro continuará hasta el 10 de noviembre, con los mejores surfistas del planeta enfrentándose a los rápidos y exigentes tubos de Cloud 9.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli's father once feared for his racing future; now his son is F1's youngest world champion
articles.summary: For Marco Antonelli, watching his son lift the Formula 1 World Championship trophy must have felt almost unreal.
articles.body: For Marco Antonelli, watching his son lift the Formula 1 World Championship trophy must have felt almost unreal. There was a time when he worried that Kimi's passion for racing could lead to the same disappointment he had experienced. His own career never reached the heights he had hoped for, and he feared his son might face similar struggles. Now, at just 20, Kimi has achieved something his father could never have imagined. The Mercedes driver has become the youngest world champion in F1 history, turning years of sacrifice and uncertainty into a remarkable family achievement.Marco Antonelli's painful racing past shaped his fears for KimiMarco's concerns were rooted in personal experience. He had pursued a professional racing career during the 1990s and came close to securing opportunities with major manufacturers. However, circumstances repeatedly worked against him.He tested for Alfa Romeo, but a change in team leadership ended that opportunity. A possible move with BMW also failed to materialise. Those setbacks left a lasting impression on him.Speaking to BBC Sport, Marco explained why he initially struggled with his son's growing interest in motorsport."Sometimes you are fast but not in the right position to become a professional driver," he said.He added: "I suffered a lot for it," Marco says. "And, of course, I was scared that my son [would] relive the same situation. At the beginning, I was very stressed about the passion my son had for motorsport."Despite those fears, Kimi's talent became increasingly difficult to ignore. He first tried karting at five and quickly showed an unusual understanding of racing.One memorable moment came when Kimi was 10. Marco allowed him to control the steering and gears of a Lamborghini while he handled the throttle and brakes. His son's ability behind the wheel left him impressed.Mercedes also recognised the youngster's potential early, signing him to its junior programme in 2018. That support helped Kimi progress through the junior categories and eventually reach Formula 1.Kimi Antonelli's F1 title brings his father's fears full circleKimi's journey was not without difficult moments. His first season with Mercedes brought intense pressure, particularly as he stepped into the seat previously occupied by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton.However, he responded with an impressive 2026 campaign and secured the championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix. His father watched the historic moment unfold before celebrating with his family.Speaking to Sky Sports F1, Marco said: "Step by step he makes himself stronger and stronger and stronger, and this is the result."He also spoke about their relationship, adding: "I'm very lucky because the relationship with my son and with my daughter is special, and this is the best thing in the world that I can have."The emotional moment became even more special when Marco recalled telling his son about the title."I said to him, I don't know if you know, you are the champion. I cried!"For a father who once feared motorsport would bring his son the same heartbreak, the championship represents much more than a sporting achievement. It is the moment those old worries finally gave way to pride.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: No Lakshya Sen, PV Sindhu at Korea Open after Hylo Open triumph; Prannoy, Tanvi lead India's challenge
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Fresh from a memorable double triumph at the Hylo Open, India's badminton stars Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu will be missing from the Korea Open,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Fresh from a memorable double triumph at the Hylo Open, India's badminton stars Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu will be missing from the Korea Open, leaving the responsibility of leading the Indian challenge to experienced HS Prannoy and emerging youngster Tanvi Sharma at the USD 500,000 Super 500 tournament beginning in Yeosu on Tuesday.Lakshya, who ended his year-long title drought with a commanding victory over Indonesia's Jonatan Christie in the men's singles final in Germany on Sunday, has withdrawn from the Korea Open despite being scheduled to face China's Dong Tian Yao in the opening round.Sindhu, who also clinched the women's singles crown at the Hylo Open with a straight-game victory over Denmark's Line Højmark Kjærsfeldt, has opted to skip the Korea Open and the subsequent Japan Masters as she looks to take a break following her title-winning campaign.The absence of both singles champions is a setback for India's campaign, but it also provides an opportunity for other players to make their mark on the international circuit.Prannoy, Tanvi lead singles challengeWith Lakshya out, former world No. 1 Prannoy will shoulder much of the responsibility in the men's singles. The 33-year-old, a bronze medallist at the 2023 World Championships, will open his campaign against South Korea's Yoo Tae Bin.Prannoy will be keen to make a deep run in a competitive men's singles draw featuring Chinese Taipei's top seed Chou Tien Chen, Japan's third seed Kodai Naraoka and Canada's Victor Lai.In women's singles, attention will be on Tanvi Sharma, who has emerged as one of India's promising young players after winning the Taipei Open earlier this year. She begins her campaign against Japan's Manami Suizu.Malvika Bansod faces a challenging opening-round assignment against fourth seed Sim Yu Jin of South Korea, while Anmol Kharb will look to build on her impressive semifinal run at the Hylo Open when she takes on Canada's Rachel Chan.The 19-year-old's performance in Germany, where she reached the last four before losing to Sindhu, will provide confidence heading into the Korean tournament.India have entries in doubles tooIndia will also have representation in the doubles events. Sonali Singh and Ritika Thaker will compete in women's doubles, taking on Australia's Laudya Chelsea Griselda and Nozomi Shimizu.In mixed doubles, Dhruv Rawat and K. Maneesha will face China's seventh seeds Zhu Yi Jun and Li Qian.With the two biggest Indian singles names sitting out after their title-winning exploits in Germany, the Korea Open presents an opportunity for Prannoy, Tanvi and the other Indian challengers to step up and keep the country's momentum going on the BWF World Tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid has a $100 million NHL career, but wife Lauren Kyle is building her own business empire through luxury design, fashion and hospitality ventures in Edmonton
articles.summary: Connor McDavid signed an eight-year, $100 million contract in 2017 and remains the face of the Edmonton Oilers.
articles.body: Connor McDavid signed an eight-year, $100 million contract in 2017 and remains the face of the Edmonton Oilers. His wife, Lauren Kyle McDavid, has spent those years building a business base in the same city. She runs a design studio started in 2019, a furniture showroom, a downtown bar and a sportswear label, and her cookbook launched on January 30. In May she confirmed plans for a second Trove location in Texas. Few hockey spouses carry a résumé this broad, and almost all of it sits in Edmonton.How Lauren Kyle built a business empire beside Connor McDavid’s $100 million careerStart with the money, because it explains why this story is unusual. McDavid’s eight-year deal paid $12.5 million a year, and in October 2025 he signed a two-year, $25 million extension at the same annual figure. It runs from 2026-27 through 2027-28. Those are US dollars. A household with that income does not need a second paycheque. Lauren Kyle McDavid says she was always headed this way anyway. “I always knew I was going to be an entrepreneur,” she told The Canadian Press in June 2025, adding that this was true before she met Connor.She grew up in Sudbury, Ontario, with two brothers who played hockey. She was never much of a fan. She studied fine arts at the University of British Columbia, then interior design at Toronto Metropolitan University, the school once known as Ryerson. Her cousin introduced her to Connor around that time.Kyle and Co. Design Studio followed in 2019. The firm designed the couple’s Edmonton home and their Muskoka cottage, which gave her a visible portfolio before she opened a single storefront. They married on July 27, 2024, on a private island on Lake Muskoka.Think of the studio as the engine. Design clients led to furniture, furniture led to a venue, and the venue led to a brand. Each step used the last one as proof.What is inside Trove Living and Bar Trove?The biggest bet is a building. Kyle McDavid and business partner Brittany Schulz leased the long-vacant Canada Permanent Building in downtown Edmonton, an Edwardian Baroque landmark. Her design studio anchors the top floor. Below it sit Trove Living, a furniture showroom of about 9,000 square feet that represents European brands, and Bar Trove, a 40-seat cocktail lounge serving small plates.Schulz had worked as an outside furniture rep for the design business, so the partnership grew out of a working relationship, not a celebrity pairing. The mix makes sense on paper. Design advice, products and a place to sit all share one address, which gives a client a reason to stay longer.The venue opened on June 6, 2025, after an influencer media night with a red carpet and a DJ. The timing was brutal. The Oilers were in the Stanley Cup Final against Florida, and Kyle McDavid watched Game 5 from a spot by the bar’s fireplace. She planned to stand there again for Game 6, in the same heels and with the same red handbag, while other Oilers partners watched on a projected wall. Florida won the series.Locals noticed anyway. Quinn Phillips of the Edmonton Downtown Business Association said, “Everything is kind of buzzing now in downtown.” Her colleague Puneeta McBryan, the group’s executive director, said a big celebrity name investing in the core is huge for the area.How Sports Club Atelier turned playoff jackets into a fashion labelSports Club Atelier started as a favour. Kyle McDavid told Daily Hive she was handed the job of making playoff jackets for the women around the Oilers, and she found she loved it. She also spotted a gap. Fans like her wanted clothes that looked good at games, and the market offered little.The label launched in 2025. Its Oilers line, the Foundry Collection of jackets and accessories, dropped before that spring’s playoffs. Hockey Canada merchandise followed. By May 2026 the brand had its NHL licence, a Liquid I.V. collaboration planned around the Montreal Grand Prix and a Stella Artois project for Wimbledon in July. She also said talks with baseball teams were under way.The jackets matter more than they look. Kyle McDavid says she designs each one imagining it hanging in her closet for her future kids. She thinks of them as markers of a year, a team and a playoff run. That sentimental angle is what separates a keepsake from merchandise.Cheri Bradish, director of the Future of Sport Lab, told The Canadian Press that Kyle McDavid’s ties to the NHL have helped her earn money from her work. Bradish also said she deserves credit for her own background in design and business. Both points can be true at once.Why Edmonton, and what comes next for Kyle McDavidWhy build all of this in Edmonton and not Toronto or Vancouver? Her answer is practical. “There’s not a huge market saturation in Edmonton for different businesses,” she told Daily Hive. She sees gaps to fill, and she says people there like new things.She is also direct about the life around it. People assume being a hockey wife is easy because the husbands are well paid, she told The Canadian Press, but she said the stress and the strain on families are real. She sees a parallel between her role and his. He captains a team, she manages employees, and both, she said, learn from mistakes by finding the gaps and fixing them.The newest product is a book. The Atelier Table launched on January 30, 2026, and runs past 300 pages. Menus are built for six and organized around occasions such as girls’ night, game day and brunch. Each comes with advice on styling the table, which ties the cookbook back to her design roots. Her spicy lobster pasta, a recipe she created herself, was set to appear on Bar Trove’s menu.Texas is the next stop. Reports so far give no address or opening date, and none of her companies has made revenue public. “Empire” describes the range of her work for now. The financials remain private.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nikita Kucherov, Dylan Larkin, Quinn Hughes and the NHL Trade Block Big Board for November 2026
articles.summary: The first month of the 2026-27 NHL regular season is history, but it also came with a pair of big trades.
articles.body:
The first month of the 2026-27 NHL regular season is history, but it also came with a pair of big trades.

A blockbuster deal occurred just before we published our October NHL Trade Block Big Board , when the Columbus Blue Jackets shipped Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies. Both had featured in our previous trade boards.

On Oct. 23, a more prominent player from our October board finally moved, as the Winnipeg Jets traded goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner topped every one of our trade boards since July.

Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin has also featured prominently on our trade boards since he went public with his trade request in June. Recent rumors suggest he could be the next noteworthy star to be moved in an early-season blockbuster, which is becoming the norm this season.

At least, that's how it looked until Oct. 30, when it was reported that Tampa Bay Lightning superstar Nikita Kucherov wouldn't sign an extension and had requested a trade.

Larkin is among the few players from our previous board to make it onto our November board. Most have dropped out of the rumor mill as speculation focused on other players throughout October. Meanwhile, Alexander Nikishin was dropped after signing a one-year deal with the Carolina Hurricanes.

Follow along to see which other notable players joined Larkin and Kucherov in the rumor mill over the past month. As always, the players' skills, experience, contracts, and likelihood of being moved factored into our compilation.

As the Vancouver Canucks rebuild their roster, Elias Pettersson has frequently appeared on our previous NHL Trade Boards . However, his declining production over the past three seasons and expensive contract made him unlikely to be dealt.

However, the 27-year-old center has looked rejuvenated this season. The Canucks are at the bottom of the standings , but his all-around performance has made him one of their few bright spots. His point-per-game production has made him their leading scorer .

On Oct. 5, Ben Kuzma of The Vancouver Province suggested Pettersson's play could improve his value in the trade market. Kuzma also felt the Swede could be worthwhile for the Canucks to retain, pointing out that he could be helpful in the development of their promising young center.

Sportsnet's Michael Amato felt that Pettersson's $11.6 million average annual value might not be as burdensome because of the rising salary cap. The limited number of available centers in the trade market could also make him more enticing as a trade candidate, provided he's willing to waive his no-movement clause.

14. Zach Werenski, Columbus Blue Jackets

Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski was the subject of trade chatter in late June following reports that he was considering his future. He was reportedly close to being shipped to the Dallas Stars until he and general manager Don Waddell released statements reiterating his commitment to the club.

That silenced the speculation for several months. However, the Blue Jackets' inconsistent performance throughout October prompted Sportsnet's Michael Amato to ponder the effect that another potentially lost season could have on the reigning Norris Trophy winner's future in Columbus.

Werenski is signed through 2027-28 , but the Blue Jackets can open extension talks next July. However, Amato thinks they're running out of time to convince the 29-year-old blueliner to stay in Columbus.

Amato envisioned a scenario where Werenski requests a trade before the March 1 trade deadline. That's a possibility worth considering if the Blue Jackets fail to rise among the playoff contenders this season.

Uncertainty over Quinn Hughes' future with the Minnesota Wild earned him a spot on our last two Trade Boards. Wild general manager Bill Guerin said in September that he would give the 27-year-old superstar defenseman all the time he needed to make his decision.

Hughes can become an unrestricted free agent next July and would be among the biggest names in the UFA market. He's in the final season of a six-year contract worth an average annual value of $7.9 million. As an elite NHL defenseman, he could command over $20 million annually on his next contract.

On Oct. 1, Wild beat writers Michael Russo and Joe Smith of The Athletic suggested that Guerin would have to consider moving Hughes by the March 1 trade deadline if he remains unsigned. It would be "the nightmare scenario," considering how much Guerin gave up in future assets to acquire Hughes last season.

Fast-forward to Oct. 27, when Guerin told a local radio station he hadn't held contract talks with Hughes for some time , adding that he wasn't going to try to beg the blueliner to sign. That won't mollify nervous Wild fans or silence the conjecture about his immediate future.

The Philadelphia Flyers' hopes of building on last season's surprising playoff appearance have crashed back to earth following a 3-8-4 record in their first 15 games . That poor start has their followers wondering what general manager Daniel Briere will do to get them back on the winning track.

On Oct. 13, Daily Faceoff's Anthony Di Marco reported that sources claimed some within the organization were frustrated over Konecny's performance. It was suggested that the 29-year-old winger could be approached about waiving his no-movement clause if the club failed to improve.

Di Marco followed up a week later, saying the Flyers had to address their logjam of wingers. While Owen Tippett drew the most interest around the league, Di Marco felt that was because of Konecny's NMC, adding that the latter had more value as the better all-around player.

However, Flyers beat writer Kevin Kurz of The Athletic considered it " incredibly unlikely " that Konecny would be traded in the near future, citing his value to the team as well as his contract and no-movement protection. Nevertheless, one can't fully dismiss the possibility given where the Flyers are right now.

Erik Karlsson frequently appeared on our NHL Trade Block Big Boards over the past two seasons, with the latest in September . At that time, the 36-year-old Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman was linked to the Ottawa Senators and Toronto Maple Leafs, depending on how the season unfolded for all three clubs.

With the Penguins struggling through October, Karlsson has resurfaced in the rumor mill. On Oct. 23, TSN's Darren Dreger reported that general manager Kyle Dubas was listening to offers on some of his veteran players, including Karlsson.

Despite his age, Karlsson could draw some interest in the trade market. He's in the final season of his contract and is having a strong offensive performance with a team-leading 16 points . However, his contract remains a major sticking point, carrying a $10 million cap hit with a full no-movement clause.

Karlsson probably won't be moved this early in the season, but that could change if the Penguins sink lower in the standings. Nevertheless, interested clubs might prefer a trade later in the season when most of his salary has been paid.

The Vancouver Canucks' rebuilding process earned winger Jake DeBrusk the No. 13 spot on our previous NHL Trade Block Big Board . Given the team's current position at the foot of the standings , he could resurface more frequently in the rumor mill as the season progresses.

DeBrusk, 30, is signed through 2030-31 . He carries an average annual value of $5.5 million, which is now an affordable rate for a top-six winger. This is the final season that he has a full no-movement clause, as it shifts to a 15-team no-trade list next July.

With eight points in 14 games, DeBrusk is off to a decent start to this season. On Oct. 12, Ben Kuzma of The Vancouver Province reported that the veteran winger was working on other aspects of his game, including doing more without the puck and using his speed more effectively on the forecheck.

Kuzma suggested that the improvement in DeBrusk's overall game could bolster his stock in the trade market. That could make him a player to watch as teams start shopping for an experienced scoring winger.

The Calgary Flames' ongoing roster rebuild put defenseman Zach Whitecloud at No. 5 on our October NHL Trade Block Big Board . His shutdown defensive game, Stanley Cup experience, and affordable $2.8 million average annual value through 2027-28 made him an enticing trade candidate.

On Oct. 15, Daily Faceoff's Mike Gould had Whitecloud atop his list of the Flames' trade assets . The extra year on his contract meant management could afford to wait for the right offers, but Gould believes the blueliner's trade value will never be higher than it is right now.

Eleven days later, The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported that Flames general manager Craig Conroy has received calls about Whitecloud. However, he doesn't want to lose the blueliner's experience and skill. He also noted that Whitecloud loves playing in Calgary and has bought into the Flames rebuild.

Conroy could re-sign Whitecloud next summer if the latter remains committed to helping the Flames. However, a significant trade offer could prove too tempting to pass up.

Trade rumors have dogged winger Rickard Rakell since the summer of 2025. The 33-year-old Pittsburgh Penguins winger earned a spot on our August NHL Trade Targets Big Board .

Given the Pittsburgh Penguins' inconsistent play through October, Rakell resurfaced in the rumor mill. On Oct. 17, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Penguins were willing to move a veteran player in exchange for draft picks.

Dan Kingerski of Pittsburgh Hockey Now speculated that Rakell could be one of those veterans. On Oct. 23, TSN's Darren Dreger mentioned that Rakell was among the veterans the Penguins were willing to move.

Rakell is signed through 2027-28 with an average annual value of $5 million. He also has an eight-team no-trade list. There's no indication yet that he'll be moved soon, but that could change if the Penguins keep struggling in the standings.

For the past two seasons, the Calgary Flames have shipped out veteran players for younger talent as part of their roster rebuild. That's why center Morgan Frost landed at the No. 10 position on our September NHL Trade Block Big Board .

Frost, 27, is in the final season of his two-year contract . He has an average annual value of $4.4 million and an eight-team no-trade list. His offensive skills could make him a tempting trade target if he plays well this season, especially given the lack of skilled centers in the trade market.

On Oct. 15, Daily Faceoff's Mike Gould placed Frost among the top tier of his ranking of the Flames' trade candidates. He cited Frost's consistency as a 40-point producer, which could draw interest from teams looking for a middle-six center.

However, The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported on Oct. 26 that Frost is in the age category where he could still have a future with the Flames. General manager Craig Conroy is interested in re-signing Frost, but could shop him at some point before the trade deadline if he intends to go to market next summer.

After exceeding expectations by reaching the playoffs last season, the Pittsburgh Penguins entered this season hoping to build on that performance. Instead, they've stumbled through the opening month and are near the bottom of the Eastern Conference .

On Oct. 17, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Penguins were willing to move a veteran forward for draft picks to provide more room for younger players. Dan Kingerski of Pittsburgh Hockey Now suggested that winger Bryan Rust could be a trade candidate.

Rust, 34, has frequently surfaced in the rumor mill since the summer of 2025, including in our August NHL Trade Targets Big Board . He's signed through 2027-28 with an average annual value of $5.13 million and lacks no-trade protection.

On Oct. 23, TSN's Darren Dreger mentioned Rust was among the players the Penguins were listening on. His lack of no-trade protection would make him easier to move than the other teammates on this list.

5. Ivan Miroshnichenko, Washington Capitals

Thanks to offseason additions Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, the Washington Capitals have considerable depth on their wings this season. However, it's also made it difficult for promising Ivan Miroshnichenko to crack the lineup.

Miroshnichenko, 22, was chosen 20th overall by the Capitals in the 2022 draft. The additions of Tuch and Kyrou, and the emergence of wingers Aliaksei Protas and Ryan Leonard, have limited him to three games this season. He's in the first year of a two-year contract worth an affordable $925,000 annually.

On Oct. 24, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Capitals permitted Miroshnichenko and his agent to speak with other NHL clubs. Four days later, Dave Pagnotta of The Fourth Period claimed that the Chicago Blackhawks, Philadelphia Flyers, Calgary Flames, and Seattle Kraken were interested.

Rebuilding teams like Chicago, Philadelphia, and Calgary can give Miroshnichenko more playing time. Meanwhile, the Kraken are on the lookout for players who can help them offensively.

4. Dmitri Voronkov, Columbus Blue Jackets

On the eve of the opening night of this regular season, the Columbus Blue Jackets traded Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for winger Matthew Knies in a blockbuster deal. However, that move did little to improve their fortunes, as their play was inconsistent in October.

Those difficulties sparked speculation that another Blue Jackets winger could be a trade candidate. On Oct. 22, Pierre LeBrun reported that some teams had called to express interest in Dmitri Voronkov.

The 26-year-old winger is slated to become a restricted free agent with arbitration rights next summer. He's in the second season of a two-year contract with an average annual value of $4.18 million. The 6'5", 230-pounder is a big, physical forward who had a career high of 23 goals and 24 assists for 47 points in 2024-25.

LeBrun couldn't say if Voronkov would be traded, but he claimed the Blue Jackets were listening. His situation bears watching as November rolls along, especially if the Jackets struggle to gain ground in the standings.

Contract talks between the Detroit Red Wings and Simon Edvinsson took an ominous turn on Oct. 3, when Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported the restricted free-agent defenseman preferred a trade.

It's been frequently reported that Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff's priority is re-signing the 23-year-old. Nevertheless, Horcoff is also reportedly fielding calls from clubs interested in the skillful young blueliner.

Pierre LeBrun claimed the Sharks and Boston Bruins were among 10 teams pursuing Edvinsson. The Hockey News ' Eric Cruickshank listed the San Jose Sharks, St. Louis Blues, and Toronto Maple Leafs as potential suitors. Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli felt he'd be a good fit with the Philadelphia Flyers.

On Oct. 30, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Sharks, Blues, Boston Bruins, Nashville Predators, and Seattle Kraken "took a long look" at Edvinsson. He also reported that the Sharks made a serious offer that was rejected by the Red Wings.

The 5 p.m. ET deadline on Dec. 1 for signing restricted free agents hangs over this situation. If Edvinsson remains unsigned by then, he'll be ineligible to play in the NHL for the remainder of the season.

The first month of this season has had its share of surprises, from the Marchenko-for-Knies blockbuster move on the eve of opening night, Connor Hellebuyck's trade to the New Jersey Devils, and Dylan Larkin sitting out on the Detroit Red Wings awaiting a trade.

However, no one saw Nikita Kucherov's trade request coming. The day before Halloween, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the 33-year-old superstar winger didn't intend to sign an extension with the Tampa Bay Lightning and asked to be traded.

A two-time Stanley Cup champion, Kucherov is also a two-time winner of the Hart Memorial Trophy (including last season) and the Ted Lindsay Award , and a three-time Art Ross Trophy winner. He's in the final season of an eight-year contract with an average annual value of $9.5 million and a 10-team trade list.

Friedman also noted a statement from Lightning general manager Julian BriseBois claiming his club "unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita." Meanwhile, The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported that Kucherov intends to continue playing with the Lightning while this situation plays out.

LeBrun's colleague Chris Johnston stated that sources claimed Kucherov sought a six-year contract extension worth a $20 million AAV. Evidently, the Lightning aren't comfortable paying that much for that long. LeBrun said his trade request is not a ploy to make the Bolts meet his price.

Despite the Lightning's statement, we can't rule out the possibility that they'll change their minds by the March 1 trade deadline. Given Kucherov's stature among the league's elite stars, his first-ever appearance on our trade boards earns him the No. 2 spot.

Following Connor Hellebuyck's trade from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils, Dylan Larkin of the Detroit Red Wings takes over the top spot on our NHL Trade Block Big Board.

Throughout October, Larkin's trade request made him a frequent subject of media speculation. On Oct. 29, the Red Wings announced they had suspended him without pay, saying he had informed the team that he would no longer play for the organization. His agent, Pat Brisson, separately said Larkin had "had enough of the situation" and had been "very professional and cooperative" throughout the process.

Larkin expanded his trade list to 10 teams in October. They include the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers, Washington Capitals, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, New Jersey Devils, Colorado Avalanche and the Tampa Bay Lightning.

According to TSN's Pierre LeBrun, the Minnesota Wild have pushed the hardest to acquire him. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that they've offered center Danila Yurov, a veteran player, and several first-round picks.

LeBrun doesn't see the Capitals as a fit, while the Panthers haven't made any inquiries. His colleague, Chris Johnston, said most of the teams on Larkin's list either have enough centers, lack salary-cap space, or don't believe that it's the right time to make that sort of move.

According to LeBrun, there are teams not on Larkin's list, like the Boston Bruins and Montreal Canadiens, that are interested in Larkin. On Oct. 31, Friedman said it's believed he could make changes to his list by removing some teams or adding others.

Stats and standings (as of Nov. 1, 2026) via NHL.com and Hockey-Reference.com . Contract and salary-cap info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Why Triple H Can't Afford to Wait for Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi at WWE WrestleMania 43
articles.summary: Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi has been inevitable since WWE WrestleMania 42 in April 2026.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi has been inevitable since WWE WrestleMania 42 in April 2026.

That was the night Reigns bested CM Punk for the World Heavyweight Championship and Femi conquered Brock Lesnar in a matter of minutes.

Femi went so far as to call out Reigns during the post-show press conference and set his sights on the prestigious prize in the process.

That promo planted the seeds for what is currently the biggest bout WWE could possibly book with their active talent. Fans assumed it would come to fruition as soon as SummerSlam, but even after Femi won the King of the Ring tournament, the company proved to have other plans and postponed it for down the road.

Since becoming the head of WWE Creative four years ago, Triple H has historically waited until the Show of Shows to deliver marquee matches and monumental moments. As it stands, all signs point to Reigns holding the World Heavyweight Championship until WrestleMania 43 and that being where Femi finally gets his shot.

However, there are several reasons why he can't afford to wait that long to pull the trigger on Reigns vs. Femi.

Femi Has No More Believable Hurdles to Overcome

Instead of immediately thrusting Oba Femi into world championship contention coming out of WrestleMania 42, WWE opted to have him resume his rivalry with Brock Lesnar, who fans were led to believe had retired from the ring following his loss to the Nigerian newcomer at 'Mania.

That also involved Femi forgoing the guaranteed title shot he earned from winning King of the Ring in order to face Lesnar in a rubber match inside Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam.

Once it became clear that WWE wasn't booking Reigns vs. Femi anytime soon, it was less of a question of how long WWE was willing to wait to get to it and more of about how they intended to kill time with Femi until then.

Putting him in a program with The Vision was a fine use of him post-SummerSlam, but that feud quickly lost a lot of steam once he beat Bronson Reed clean at Money in the Bank. His Sunday Night's Main Event encounter with Bron Breakker ended in a disqualification, so while they could run it back at some point, Breakker appears to be busy with the World Tag Team Championship for the foreseeable future.

The Raw roster lacks credible heels and believable opponents in general for Femi at the moment. Femi spending his time working with really anyone but Reigns going forward would make zero storyline sense for someone who has called out Reigns on more than one occasion.

Reigns' Matches Will Become More and More Predictable

Roman Reigns' recent World Heavyweight Championship defense against LA Knight at Money in the Bank was an overall exceptional outing with an electric atmosphere in New Orleans. The biggest thing it suffered from was the end result being so predictable.

From the moment Reigns took the title from CM Punk at WrestleMania 42, it was essentially set in stone that he wouldn't be dropping it to anyone but Oba Femi, regardless of when that was. Reigns' comments during the 'Mania post-show press conference about being around for the summer indicated that SummerSlam might mark the end of his reign, but that didn't end up being the case.

In all fairness, The Tribal Chief has been having a heck of a run as champ this year. All of his matches have had a big fight feel and the clean finishes have been a refreshing change of pace compared to the excessive amount of Bloodline interference during his previous reign.

It's been difficult for fans to buy into the idea of Reigns actually losing knowing that the Femi match remains on the horizon. Realistically, he could drop the belt briefly and get it back in time for WrestleMania 43, but Triple H has long been high on uninterrupted championship runs as well as ensuring Reigns looks strong.

Royce Keys could challenge for the World Heavyweight title in the coming months, and it'd be booking malpractice for him not to, but he's automatically an afterthought if Femi is the final boss at 'Mania.

WWE Runs the Risk of Fans Souring on Femi Before WrestleMania

Speaking of Superstars who are booked to look too strong, WWE has had a longstanding issue of that throughout its history, specifically with anyone being built up as the next top babyface of the top company.

It's what eventually caused fans to turn against Hulk Hogan at the height of his WWE run, John Cena infamously had a polarizing relationship with crowds during his time on top, and Reigns was never truly accepted by the audience until well into his heel run a few years ago.

Even Cody Rhodes is now approaching a point where fans are ready to see him break bad, but that's at least after years of being portrayed as "the guy" and having them mostly behind him.

Femi hasn't won a world championship on the main roster yet and WWE is running the risk of fans souring on him before then by booking him to be so unstoppable.

The sole loss he's endured so far was to Brock Lesnar at Clash in Italy. Otherwise, he's hardly been made to look vulnerable, and that could come back to bite him with it being so obvious that he'll be dethroning Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship once they go one-on-one.

Putting the title on Femi anytime soon would not be "rushing" him into a spot he can't excel in. In fact, he could have been world champ coming out of WrestleMania 42 and fans very likely wouldn't have rebelled because it would've been something new and he's already world champion material.

In other words, it wouldn't be completely out of the question for fans to be split for Femi vs. Reigns come WrestleMania.

Reigns Can't Keep Ignoring the Elephant in the Room

As noted, Femi has now called out Reigns and the World Heavyweight Championship not once but twice in post-show press conferences: first at WrestleMania 42 and again at Money in the Bank.

That's what makes it all the more puzzling that Femi has been focused on everyone but Reigns for the past six months.

Winning King of the Ring should have been his ticket to the main event scene, but he threw that title shot away so he could avenge his loss to Lesnar at SummerSlam. WWE continues to call him King of the Ring, but the implication is that his title shot is now null and void and that he'll have to earn another opportunity some other way.

Engaging in a blood feud with Lesnar was understandable to an extent, but he gains nothing from racking up wins against a dead faction in The Vision. He also wouldn't benefit from challenging for or capturing the Intercontinental Championship, either.

If anything, Reigns ignoring Femi's demands for a match makes Femi look less than. It sends the message that Reigns is too busy with worthier opponents and his ongoing rivalry with The 946 to be bothered by The Ruler name-dropping him every so often.

It will be a big deal when they do cross paths down the road, but the teases of their looming match haven't been subtle. Thus, it's illogical to get fans hyped for it when it's still many months away.

There Are Other Potential Matches for Both Men at WrestleMania

The main question fans might ask if WWE were to run Reigns vs. Femi ahead of WrestleMania 43 is what the two of them would do at the event instead.

Of course, their first match could take place at the Royal Rumble followed by a rematch at WrestleMania (assuming Reigns were to somehow successfully retain at the Rumble), but on the surface, that wouldn't be an exciting direction to go in. It'd merely be delaying the inevitable.

The Bloodline not factoring into virtually any of Reigns' matches this year has to amount to something, ideally the group turning on their Tribal Chief when Reigns loses to Femi decisively. Femi defeating Reigns at the Rumble could lay the groundwork for Reigns vs. Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania with Fatu finally getting that elusive victory over Reigns.

Femi could then walk into WrestleMania as World Heavyweight champion and defend against a fresh face such as Bron Breakker or someone from SmackDown like Cody Rhodes or CM Punk. There are no shortage of Superstars he can face on The Grandest Stage of Them All if Reigns was tied up in a non-title affair.

Above all else, Reigns' crowning moment doesn't need to be validated by being saved for 'Mania. The Triple H regime must stop waiting for the tentpole premium live events to pay off certain stories and deliver key matches and moments as it makes everything else inconsequential in the meantime.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Dream Unrivaled Trios We'd Like to See in 2027
articles.summary: Before you know it, the third season of Unrivaled will be ready to tip off, and with that, it is almost time to draft. As the rosters refresh going into the 2027 season, new faces are ready to take the league by storm.
articles.body:
Before you know it, the third season of Unrivaled will be ready to tip off, and with that, it is almost time to draft. As the rosters refresh going into the 2027 season, new faces are ready to take the league by storm.

Some of the new entries are players coming off impressive WNBA rookie seasons such as Olivia Miles, Flau'jae Johnson, or Kiki Rice. Others are players who have already stamped their pro careers, such as Gabby Williams or Jessica Shepard. Regardless of their background, they are ready to shake up Unrivaled as we know it.

Ahead of the official Unrivaled draft on November 4th, these are some trios that would be electric on the court together.

Dream Trio : Paige Bueckers, Aaliyah Edwards, Allisha Gray

Paige Bueckers showed up to Unrivaled last year and immediately became one of the most productive forces in the entire league. Averaging 22.1 points, 6.1 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, Bueckers dominated across the board.

Putting Bueckers with another dominant three-level scorer in Allisha Gray, who averaged 21.8 points per game last season, would create a largely impossible task for opposing defenses to stop.

You round out the trio by reuniting Bueckers with her college teammate Aaliyah Edwards. Edwards has been able to put her best professional play on display in Unrivaled, including great showings in the 1-on-1 Tournament both years. She would be perfectly set up to feast off of the attention required on Bueckers and Gray.

Dream Trio: Sonia Citron, Brittney Sykes, Gabby Williams

Best of luck to anyone trying to pass around this trio. While Sonia Citron, Brittney Sykes and Gabby Williams can all certainly get buckets, the entertainment of this group is what it would be like watching anyone try to score on them.

Some of the world's top defensive players have already taken the court in Unrivaled. Williams' decision to join the league brings arguably the best defender in the world to the 3-on-3 league. Notably, the style of play will have Williams often matched up with an offensive player on an island. Don't expect anyone to look forward to seeing her across the way.

Citron didn't have the strongest year from three in her first Unrivaled season, shooting 21.4%, but she's certainly shown she can be a dominant scorer. Sykes dealt with injuries in the WNBA season but looked on track to be a WNBA All-Star early in the year and was great in Unrivaled last season. This team would be on the attack non-stop on both ends of the floor. The style of play would be electric.

Dream Trio: Jackie Young, Arike Ogunbowale, Jessica Shepard

Arike Ogunbowale ended last year's Unrivaled season alongside her Mist BC teammates hoisting a championship. The trio of Ogunbowale, Jackie Young and Jessica Shepard keeps that title feeling alive. The last time the trio played together ended with Notre Dame winning the 2018 NCAA Championship in historic fashion.

We have seen Ogunbowale and Shepard reunite in the WNBA this season, but adding Jackie Young to the trio brings balance that can be super fun in the Unrivaled setting. Shepard's ability as a playmaker, averaging over five assists for the Wings this season, can make for unique pace-pushing and half-court movement for this trio.

Both Ogunbowale and Young have had their games translate to Unrivaled pretty seamlessly. Young saw immense growth in her playmaking during her play for the Aces this WNBA season. Her translating that next to Ogunbowale would give both players space to get buckets.

Angel Reese's stats in entire postseason run

Dream Trio: Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray, Marina Mabrey

This trio is centered around Chelsea Gray. The "Point Gawd" has stamped her name in women's basketball history by reading defenses and making the right choice. Surrounding her with players like Napheesa Collier and Marina Mabrey gives her solutions to any issue the defense might cause.

Marina Mabrey was a flamethrower last year in Unrivaled, leading the league with 25.3 points per game. That was headlined by setting a league single-game scoring record of 47 points in front of an incredible Philadelphia crowd. After a similarly dominant scoring season for the Toronto Tempo, all signs point to Mabrey keeping her scoring form this season.

Napheesa Collier missed all of last Unrivaled season, but after getting her feet under her with a gold medal at the FIBA World Cup, the potential of a true return to form feels likely. When she is in that form, Collier is simply one of the best players in the world. Pairing Chelsea Gray, who averaged 24.2 points per game, only behind Mabrey's league-leading mark last season, with these two would create an immensely high-powered offense.

Dream Trio: Breanna Stewart, Kayla McBride, Kiki Rice

If you have Breanna Stewart on your team, you have a chance to win a championship. It's been that simple for a very long time. Her ability to do whatever is asked and do it at a superstar level is incomparable.

It takes different forms, but Kayla McBride and Kiki Rice are similar players in their versatility. McBride is known for her three-point shooting but is an incredibly underrated defender. For the Lynx, she is consistently asked to guard the opponent's best perimeter player while also contributing on offense. Although McBride missed last year's Unrivaled season, her production was strong in 2025, averaging 22.4 points per game and being named to the All-Unrivaled First Team.

Kiki Rice has been a similar player throughout her career at UCLA and now in the WNBA with the Tempo. There is just a constant feeling of impact on the game from Rice whenever she is on the court. It can be scoring on one possession, a rebound on the next, then a stifling defensive stop. That versatility will be super important as she adjusts to the Unrivaled style of play. The unique skills of these three allow for a lot of freedom and complementary basketball.

Dream Trio: Shakira Austin, Olivia Miles, Dominique Malonga

Olivia Miles plays with a flair few have ever shown in basketball. 3-on-3 basketball could be the stage to showcase that even more as she enters her debut Unrivaled season.

With the Lynx, it has been her partnerships in the pick-and-roll that have allowed Miles to shine most, so why not pair her with two of the most exciting bigs in Unrivaled? Shakira Austin followed up a great Unrivaled campaign with an incredible season with the Mystics. Austin had a strong argument to be the WNBA's Most Improved Player, finishing second behind Jessica Shepard. Pairing her with Miles can add even more elements to her game.

Adding Dominique Malonga to this trio opens up several possibilities. Malonga can show more of her perimeter play, which she's flashed but hasn't fully developed. She also can create an oppressive defense down low with Austin. Selfishly, the audacity of Miles' passing might give Unrivaled fans the best chance to see an alley-oop to Malonga, which everyone would want to see.

Dream Trio: Rhyne Howard, Flau'jae Johnson, Kelsey Plum

Kelsey Plum has a world-class ability to microwave points. That showed during the last Unrivaled season. Averaging 22.6 points per game in just under 19 minutes showcased her quick-fire productivity. Notably, the key growth in her game, which largely started in Unrivaled, has been her playmaking.

In Unrivaled last season, Plum averaged five assists per game. That growth continued as she shifted to primarily point guard duties in the WNBA prior to injuries derailing her season. Putting Plum next to two players in Rhyne Howard and Flau'jae Johnson would match the energy and style she brings perfectly.

This trio has built their games on the athleticism they possess and the effort they are willing to give. On top of that foundation is a mountain of continuously growing skill. With the Unrivaled pace of play, this would be a blink and you miss trio, as they would be up and down the court in a blur.

articles.title: Predicting WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Winners, Surprise Returns and Bold Booking Calls
articles.summary: WWE returns to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday for Crown Jewel, a premium live event that will pit the top men's and women's champions against each other in marquee matchups.
articles.body:
WWE returns to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday for Crown Jewel, a premium live event that will pit the top men's and women's champions against each other in marquee matchups.

Who will emerge victorious from the night's biggest bouts, what surprises might the company have in store, and which bold booking decisions will have fans buzzing in the show's aftermath?

Find out with this preview of the international PLE.

World Tag Team Championship: Penta and Je'Von Evans vs. The Vision

World tag team champion Bron Breakker has regained considerable momentum of late, looking like the unstoppable ass-kicker most expected him to be upon his return post-WrestleMania 42.

He steamrolled Evans at Money in the Bank, then shoved him off a ladder and through the roof of an ambulance.

This is a rare case in which, for The Badass to sustain that momentum as a top star on Raw, he needs to drop the tag team titles and eventually distance himself from the rest of The Vision.

Penta and Evans are red-hot right now, with the former possessing the Money in the Bank briefcase, and losing to them would do no damage to Breakker at all, especially with Austin Theory available to take the pin.

This feels like the perfect opportunity to move the titles to Penta and Evans while protecting Breakker and setting up his eventual singles push.

Prediction: Evans and Penta win the titles

Last Man Standing: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton

Rhodes has to win here, and he has to do it by punting Orton in the head. Anything less, and the entire months-long rivalry has served no purpose.

If Rhodes fends off the urge to turn to the dark side to defeat The Viper, he essentially becomes John Cena. As great as he is, the last thing any fan of any age needs is another vanilla babyface who does the right thing at all times.

WWE relied on that formula for two decades, and now is not the time to go back there. Especially when The American Nightmare badly needs to prove he is a man of his word and follows through with his threats.

Anything less would damage Rhodes' relationship with the fans.

Orton got the better of his rival at Sunday Night's Main Event and has taunted him ever since. The Last Man Standing match in Riyadh has to be the end of the feud, with Rhodes exorcising the demon that is The Legend Killer from his life and moving on.

Prediction: Rhodes wins with two Cross Rhodes and a punt to the skull

WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green vs. Women's World Champion Liv Morgan

The biggest winner Saturday night may well be Tiffany Stratton, whose Money in the Bank cash-in attempts have ramped up, typically a sign that a genuine cash-in is drawing near.

While that may imply Morgan is in trouble, based on recent creative decisions, it would likely result in a bad night for Green in Riyadh.

After all, everything with this second Stratton briefcase run has mimicked her first, including a show-closing cash-in tease on Monday's Raw that was beat-for-beat the same as one from two years earlier.

If that trend continues, the cash-in will be accompanied by a shocking betrayal.

Morgan will defeat Green in their inter-promotional matchup thanks to interference from The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez. Stratton will then appear to come to Green's rescue, only to betray her, cash in Money in the Bank and win her second WWE Women's Championship—one of two bold booking decisions we predict for the event.

Prediction: Morgan beats Green, and Stratton cashes in

Why Triple H Can't Wait on Reigns vs. Femi 😮‍💨

World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns vs. Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn

Reigns and Zayn rekindle their epic story Saturday in Riyadh in a battle between the top two champions in WWE today.

The Tribal Chief has been extraordinary in 2026, delivering his best in-ring performances to date and remaining undefeated along the way. He has been on another level, to the point that a loss to Zayn in Saudi Arabia seems unfathomable.

Except, The OTC and his Bloodline are in the midst of a rivalry with The 946 that is destined to culminate at Survivor Series: WarGames. This is the right opportunity to give Zayn a victory over Reigns, thanks to interference from Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Prince, Carmelo Hayes and Jaida Parker.

If Zayn going over is not enough of a bold booking decision, perhaps the arrival of The 946 brings with it the return of Jacob Fatu, with the distraction playing into Reigns' loss.

Having won his biggest matches without help, The Head of the Table would likely need to be heavily outnumbered for a defeat to feel credible.

Prediction: Zayn wins amid plenty of interference in a chaotic main event

articles.title: El 'niño prodigio' español de tenis de mesa brilla en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud
articles.standfirst: A sus 13 años, Ladimir Mayorov ya está en octavos de la competición
articles.summary: A sus 13 años, Ladimir Mayorov ya está en octavos de la competición
articles.body: El 20 de julio cumplió 13 años pero, con la pala en la mano, Ladimir Mayorov se transforma. En los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud, que se celebran en Dakar, la joven promesa española del tenis de mesa sigue asombrando al mundo. Este lunes se ha clasificado para disputar los octavos de final. El palista español se ha impuesto al luxemburgués Aaron Sahr por 3-1 (11-4, 11-9, 6-11, 15-13) en un igualado encuentro que comenzó venciendo los dos primeros juegos. Su rival recortó distancias adjudicándose el tercero, pero Mayorov logró la victoria en un ajustadísima cuarta manga. Este triunfo le sitúa segundo de grupo y se clasifica para las eliminatorias directas. En los dos enfrentamientos anteriores Ladimir había conseguido una victoria frente al senegalés Amador Ferrer y una derrota ante el surcoreano Seungsoo Lee. Este mismo año ha ganado tres medallas en el Campeonato de Europa para Jóvenes de Gondomar (Portugal): oro en dobles masculino y dobles mixto y bronce individual. El catalán, de padre ucraniano y madre rusa, milita en el Tenis Taula Cassà, en la localidad gerundense de Cassà de la Selva, donde empezó a cosechar medallas en categorías inferiores desde muy pronto, como el campeonato de España prebenjamín en 2022. La pasión de Mamorov por el tenis de mesa le viene de familia. Sus padres Eduard y Svetlana fueron jugadores profesionales. De hecho, se conocieron en los Europeos de Bratislava (Eslovaquia) en 1996. En el año 2000, se instalaron en España, primero en Cartagena (Murcia) y posteriormente en Calella (Barcelona). En la actualidad, su entrenador es su progenitor.

articles.title: FIDE Rankings: R Praggnanandhaa only Indian chess player in world's top 10; where is Gukesh?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: FIDE, the world chess body, has released its November 2026 world rankings, with R Praggnanandhaa remaining the only Indian in the Open Top 10
articles.body: NEW DELHI: FIDE, the world chess body, has released its November 2026 world rankings, with R Praggnanandhaa remaining the only Indian in the Open Top 10 at World No. 7. Grandmaster Nihal Sarin has broken into the world's top 20 for the first time, reaching a career-best World No. 19 in the latest FIDE rankings.His impressive performance at the 41st European Chess Club Cup in Budva, Montenegro, played a major role in the rise.Nihal scored 5 points from six games, won the individual gold medal on board two and added 11 rating points to reach a classical rating of 2720.India's presence in the world rankingsIndia continues to have a strong presence in international chess, with 13 players featuring in the Open Top 100. R Praggnanandhaa leads the Indian contingent at World No. 7 with a rating of 2763, followed by Arjun Erigaisi at No. 12 and Viswanathan Anand at No. 14.Nihal's rise puts him at No. 19, while reigning world champion D Gukesh is ranked 26th with 2710 points.Other notable movers include Pentala Harikrishna and Karthikeyan Murali, who each gained 11 rating points and climbed to World No. 57 and No. 58 respectively. On the other hand, Leon Luke Mendonca lost 12 points and dropped out of the world's top 100.In the women's rankings, India has 11 players in the Top 100. Koneru Humpy remains the country's highest-ranked woman at World No. 9 with 2520 points, followed by Divya Deshmukh at No. 12 and R Vaishali at No. 24.Harika Dronavalli is ranked 26th. The biggest setback came for Deekshitha Modipalli, who lost 87 rating points across three tournaments and fell from World No. 29 to No. 87.India remains second among chess nationsAt the federation level, India continues to hold the second position in all three categories: Open, Women's and Mixed.In the Open rankings, the USA leads with an average rating of 2719, while India follows at 2706. articles.summary: Winnipeg Jets head coach Scott Arniel described his team's 7-0 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes as \"embarrassing\" but emphasized he is focused on preparing his players, not on job security. The Jets face mounting pressure as they experience their ninth consecutive loss, raising questions about the coaching situation.
articles.body: The Winnipeg Jets dropped their ninth consecutive game, getting shut out 7-0 by the Carolina Hurricanes on Sunday. “Embarrassing,” was how head coach Scott Arniel described the performance after the lopsided loss, but he said he wasn’t thinking about his job security.The loss raised new questions about Winnipeg’s direction, especially after the Hurricanes scored five goals against Stuart Skinner before adding two more against replacement goaltender Clay Stevenson. Arniel also urged his players to take responsibility for their performances.Scott Arniel responds after Winnipeg Jets’ loss to Carolina HurricanesScott Arniel acknowledged the severity of the Winnipeg Jets' 7-0 loss but said his immediate responsibility was getting the team ready rather than worrying about his job as head coach.The loss to the defending Stanley Cup champions was the ninth straight for Winnipeg. The result also put more focus on the coaching staff, as the team could not find a response during a tough stretch.The Winnipeg Jets couldn't stay within striking distance of the Carolina Hurricanes all Sunday. The Hurricanes got off to an early start, putting a lot of pressure on Winnipeg’s goaltending and making it a one-sided affair.Stuart Skinner was replaced after allowing five on 17 shots. Clay Stevenson came on in relief but gave up two more goals before the final whistle, and the Jets fell 7-0. Arniel was not discounting the performance when he spoke after the game.He called the loss an “embarrassing” one for the organization and said he understood the disappointment around the team’s performance. It was a particularly disturbing loss as it was Winnipeg’s ninth consecutive loss.“Not on my mind,” he said. “I've been in this game a long, long time; that's beyond my control. My job is to get these players ready to go.”His answer suggested he wasn’t letting speculation about his future get in the way of the immediate challenge of improving Winnipeg’s performances. But Arniel also understood that once the games started, having the team ready was not all that mattered.Why did Scott Arniel demand more responsibility from players?The coaching staff is working on preparing the players, but he expects the team to take responsibility during the games, Arniel said.“I'm doing everything I possibly can with my coaching staff to get these guys ready to go, but once the puck drops... these guys also have to take some responsibility as well,” he said.The commentary was about the players' performance as Winnipeg tries to break its losing streak. The head coach took responsibility for preparation, but his comments made it clear that execution on the ice matters, too.Could Winnipeg Jets consider a coaching change?The nine-game losing streak and the magnitude of Sunday’s loss should only lead to more questions about the team’s coaching situation. But Arniel's comments alone don't prove Winnipeg is preparing to make a change.The Jets’ immediate task is to regroup on the ice and end the losing streak. Another poor showing could crank up the pressure on the organization to think about how it does things.Arniel, for now, has said publicly he is focused on getting the players ready. articles.summary: Floyd Mayweather looks to shake the rust off before challenging Ryan Garcia the WBC belt early next year.
articles.body:
I'm losing count of all of the fights Floyd Mayweather has been announced in over the last year, and while none of them have actually happened thus far, the recent talk has been about a potential WBC welterweight title fight against current champion Ryan Garcia .

Garcia has openly called for the fight with Floyd apparently amendable, but Floyd's also no dummy about this sport and business. At age 49 and not having had an actual professional boxing match in about a decade Floyd is not about to just jump straight into the ring against the 28-year-old champion, and has thereby announced he'll be taking on Matty Floyd in a December 19 exhibition bout in Bangkok, which he says will serve as a tune-up to the Garcia fight in February 2027.

In recent memory Floyd has also been announced for fights against Mike Tyson , Mike Zambidis , a Manny Pacquiao rematch, but none of those have taken place and aren't imminent, to say the least. For now, we'll just have to see if this story line actually leads somewhere going forward.

articles.title: Red Wings Reveal ‘Hometown Remix’ Uniforms
