articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings are bringing a new look to Hockeytown!

On Monday, the Red Wings unveiled their new "Hometown Remix" uniforms , featuring a fresh twist on the franchise's iconic red-and-white design.

The biggest change? The word "HOCKEYTOWN" is displayed prominently across the chest, with Detroit's legendary Winged Wheel logo positioned underneath.

The uniforms retain the traditional red base, white sleeves, and familiar color scheme that have defined the franchise for generations.

Red Wings Join NHL's Hometown Remix Program

The new look is part of the NHL's league-wide Hometown Remix initiative , which features special-edition uniforms for all 32 teams during the 2026-27 season.

Created in partnership with Fanatics, the collection celebrates each franchise's city, fan base, and local culture.

For Detroit, the inspiration is obvious: Hockeytown.

The design represents another addition to the franchise's uniform history after the Red Wings unveiled special Centennial uniforms for their 100th anniversary last season.

As we previously reported during Detroit's Centennial celebration , the organization has continued incorporating its storied history into special uniforms and commemorative designs.

Detroit also introduced a new jersey patch partner earlier this season , making the Hometown Remix collection the latest uniform-related development.

The design had already generated discussion after images resembling the new uniforms circulated online in late October.

Some fans appreciated the addition of the Hockeytown lettering, while others hoped Detroit would take a more adventurous approach.

Now that the design has been revealed, Red Wings fans can decide for themselves whether the new uniforms are a hit.

What do you think, Hockeytown? Love them or hate them?

articles.title: Ravens’ immediate QB options after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
articles.summary: The Ravens need quarterback help right away after injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Here are their options.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens lost their starting and backup quarterbacks during Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills with just four days until a Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, and Tyler Huntley is being evaluated for a turf toe injury that could sideline him for a week or longer.

Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished Sunday's game under center but took several hits behind a porous offensive line. He expressed optimism about his ability to face the Jaguars, which would be his first career NFL start, albeit in unlikely and adverse circumstances.

Fagnano's backup, though, remains to be determined. The Ravens currently do not have another quarterback on their 53-man roster or practice squad and will have to make a signing right away to get him up to speed by Thursday night. A potential multi-game absence from Huntley could even inspire Eric DeCosta to sign multiple passer should the injuries continue to accrue.

Entering Week 8 of the regular season, the pickings are about as slim as they get. The Ravens can easily find passers to get them through the coming weeks, but to keep their playoff hopes alive, they might have to consider a more aggressive move. Here are Baltimore's top quarterback options:

In the most immediate future, the Ravens need a quarterback who knows Declan Doyle's offense well enough to play on Thursday night if needed. Austin Reed spent last offseason with Doyle in Chicago and part of this year's training camp in Baltimore, making him a likely signing. He has never played in a regular-season game, though, and he would profile as little more than depth in case of another injury.

Josh Johnson, who has two previous stints in Baltimore, could also be signed off the Bengals' practice squad. He has not spent any time under Doyle, nor his two mentors, Sean Payton and Ben Johnson, but the 40-year-old journeyman is known for his ability to quickly pick up new offenses. He would give the Ravens a more veteran option under center should Fagnano falter.

And then there's – brace yourself – Cooper Rush. His disastrous spell as Jackson's backup in 2025 loomed large after narrowly missing the playoffs, but he has some level of familiarity with the offensive personnel, if not the scheme. But if Rush is bad enough to be cut by the Falcons, who have fielded Michael Penix, Tua Tagovaioloa, and undrafted rookie Jack Strand this year…

Outside of a street free agent, the Ravens could also poach a quarterback off another team's practice squad. That could bring Baltimore back to Will Levis. The ex-Titan, now-Jet was reportedly under consideration during the run-up to the 2023 draft before Jackson agreed to his contract extension. Levis' time in Tennessee was filled with turnovers – often accompanied by his comical freeze-frame reactions – and he would likely only bring more chaos to Baltimore's current mess of an offense.

Payton's Broncos do not have a quarterback on their practice squad, while the Bears and the Lions – Johnson's current and last team – only have rookies. But Hendon Hooker spent two (albeit unsuccessful) years under Johnson in Detroit and could brought in from Tennessee to learn a similar system. The former third-round pick has only thrown five regular-season passes in his career, all in 2024 at the end of Lions blowouts.

It's worth mentioning the potential for DeCosta to trade for a quarterback, though that probably is not a solution to the team's immediate needs on Thursday night. Tyson Bagent and Sam Ehlinger, who have spent time with Doyle in Chicago and Denver, respectively, could both be options. Getting Anthony Richardson from the Colts would be an ambitious and exciting move. And are the Ravens desperate enough to see what the Bengals would demand to bring Joe Flacco home to Baltimore?

Jimmy Garoppolo seemed headed for retirement this offseason, especially after his former coaches in Los Angeles and Arizona went in other directions at quarterback. But he remained interested in playing with multiple links to the Giants as recently as last month. That would add a thin layer of irony if he were to sign in Baltimore after all of the Ravens who followed John Harbaugh to New York this offseason.

Garoppolo appeared in three games for the Rams last season, but he has not thrown a regular-season pass since Week 18 of the 2024 season. He turns 35 years old today; how much does his arm have left?

Russell Wilson did officially announce his retirement this offseason. But his arm, it seems, might still have some life:

After seeing him nonchalantly drill the crossbar from 25 yards out in street clothes, you're telling me DangerRuss couldn't run play action and launch some moonballs to Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman? And, as Wilson so conveniently mentions, he does have some familiarity with Payton's offense – and thereby Doyle's. It was a terrible fit for his skillset, but, hey, knowledge is power, right?

articles.title: Florida State president listened to everyone before firing Mike Norvell. Even social media
articles.summary: Florida State president Richard McCullough detailed what went into the decision to fire Mike Norvell, which included reading fan posts on social media
articles.body:
Mike Norvell was fired as Florida State's football coach on Sunday, Nov. 1, one day after a 36-24 home loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5 this season under their seventh-year head coach.

One of the men tasked with ousting him said the decision to move on from Norvell didn't come just from university power-brokers.

Speaking with reporters hours after Norvell was sacked, Florida State president Richard McCullough delved into the factors that contributed to the move and discussed the voices that were taken into consideration when evaluating how to proceed with the future of a proud program looking to navigate the modern college football landscape.

To McCullough, that group of voices includes social media.

"Of course, we listen to everything that people are saying; all of you, we listen to the fans, even the people on social media," McCullough said . "I even read that. I don't know why I do that. I read all the emails. I respond to them if we can. I talk to my trustees. I talk to my biggest boosters and donors. I talk to football staff. I talk to other presidents at other universities that have done this kind of stuff before."

Much of what he encountered on social media was undoubtedly supportive of getting rid of Norvell, who led Florida State to an undefeated regular season in 2023 before going 10-22 since the start of the 2024 season. He didn't even have to limit his research to the internet: Before last Saturday's loss to Clemson, a plane flew over Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida calling for Norvell's firing .

Norvell entered this season on one of the hottest seats in college football. That heat momentarily cooled off after a 3-2 start capped off by a 38-7 thrashing of Virginia. Since then, the Seminoles have lost three consecutive games. Norvell is owed a buyout of roughly $50 million, though there's offset language in his contract that chips away at what the school has to pay him should the 45-year-old coach get a new job elsewhere.

2026 college football coaching changes: Every coach fired this season

The move comes at a critical time for Florida State. The Seminoles are one of the most decorated programs in the sport over the past 40 years, but outside of a two-year window in the middle of Norvell's tenure, from 2022-23, they've largely struggled over the past decade, going 59-59 since the start of the 2017 season.

Those struggles have come as their conference, the ACC, is on increasingly tenuous footing, with some of the conference's biggest brands, including Florida State, publicly expressing interest in leaving the league.

It's one of many reasons why McCullough understands the weight of what awaits him and other school leaders as they look to replace Norvell.

"This is a very complicated decision," McCullough said . "Obviously we've been evaluating this for a very long time, and you know this is a big business decision. It's the future, the fate of Florida State football. It's the legacy that we have at Florida State and trying to get it right. And that demands excellence on the field and a trajectory going in the right direction. I just did not see that trajectory, and yesterday was a bit of a defining moment for me."

"You have to take into account, including financial, everything from financial to the fan base and everything in between," McCullough later added . "We're all aligned on our decision here. At the end of the day, I'm the president of the university, and I make the decision. And that was the decision that I made."

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball Waiver Wire Week 3: Aday Mara is ready to shine
articles.summary: Rookie big man Aday Mara headlines our top fantasy basketball adds ahead of Week 3.
articles.body:
Injuries plagued the first week of the NBA season, and the hits just kept coming in Week 2.

Anthony Edwards , Ja Morant , Tyrese Haliburton , Jaren Jackson Jr. , Chet Holmgren, and Kawhi Leonard will all miss multiple weeks with injuries, opening the door for other players to take on expanded roles.

With injuries to star players piling up, I've put together my top waiver wire adds heading into Week 3.

Waiver wire adds are based on 8-cat scoring, and roster percentages come from Yahoo! leagues. Only players rostered in 50% or less will be included.

Others to consider: Derrick Jones Jr. (26%), Isaiah Jackson (24%), Cam Spencer (12%), Nolan Traore (9%), Ziaire Williams (9%), Keon Ellis (7%), Marcus Smart (3%), Kobe Sanders (2%)

Ja'Kobe Walter, Toronto Raptors (40 percent rostered)

Kawhi Leonard is injured … again. That means Walter - who has started each of the last four games with Leonard sidelined - should be a fixture in the first unit indefinitely.

Since joining the starting lineup, Walter has averaged 14 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.3 steals, 0.5 swats and 3.5 triples while shooting 50% from the floor and 80% from the charity stripe.

Walter is a three-and-D specialist who's provided Top-75 value over his last four games. This is likely the last week his roster percentage will be 40% or less until Leonard returns.

Collin Gillespie, Phoenix Suns (40 percent rostered)

Phoenix doesn't have a true PG in the starting five, but they have a Sixth Man who can run the show. Gillespie's 26.5 minutes per game are fifth most on the team and lead the Suns' bench.

In his last game out, Gillespie posted a 16/3/10 line with four steals, a block and four triples across 33 minutes. He's got big upside as a specialist in assists, steals and three-pointers. Even if he continues to come off the bench, Gillespie should see more than enough run to be a viable option in standard leagues.

Aday Mara, Oklahoma City Thunder (35 percent rostered)

The hits kept coming for OKC over the last week. After losing Jalen Williams to a gruesome leg injury, the Thunder got news that Chet Holmgren will be sidelined for 8-10 weeks after getting treatment on a patellar tendon tear.

Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Alex Caruso (ankle) are out indefinitely, and suddenly the Thunder's rotation is razor thin. Mara saw a season-high 28 minutes in his last game out, posting a 7/9/3 line with four blocked shots.

The rookie has the upside to average a double-double with multiple swats, and he's still available in 65% of Yahoo! leagues. Scoop him up while you still can.

Pelle Larsson, Miami Heat (34 percent rostered)

Like Gillespie, Larsson has carved out a meaningful role as Miami's Sixth Man, logging a career-high 29.5 minutes per game. Larsson started the season with muted production across his first two games, but he's posted strong numbers over his last four.

In that span, the Arizona product has averaged 15.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.3 triples while shooting 59.4% from the floor and 86% from the charity stripe. Miami plays four games in Week 3, which is just another reason to add Larsson.

Derrick Jones Jr., Los Angeles Clippers (26 percent rostered)

"Airplane Mode" has taken off for LA this season, averaging career highs in points (12), rebounds (4.4), assists (1.6), triples (2.4), steals (1.4) and minutes (29). He's also swatting 0.6 shots per tilt.

Jones Jr. has started every game for the Clippers, and given the roster's lack of depth, he should see minutes in the high 20's to low 30's for the foreseeable future. He's ranked just outside the fifth round in per-game fantasy value.

DJJ injured his knee in Sunday's loss to the Warriors, and if he's forced to miss time, Kobe Sanders (2%) would be worth streaming until he returns.

Jaxson Hayes, Utah Jazz (21 percent rostered)

Jusuf Nurkic is still out, and Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for 6-8 weeks. That leaves Utah with a gaping hole in its frontcourt and Hayes with a sizable opportunity.

Over his last two games (both starts), Hayes averaged 4.5 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 blocked shots across 28.5 minutes. He won't score much, but Hayes is a solid source of rebounds and defensive stats.

De'Andre Hunter, Sacramento Kings (29 percent rostered)

Hunter started the season out slowly, averaging just 5.7 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 triples on 37.5% shooting across 25 minutes over his first three games.

Over his last three, Hunter has averaged 22.3 points, 4.7 boards, 3.7 triples and a "stock" across 34 minutes per game. Hunter has shot 52.3% in that span, and he ranks 65th in per-game fantasy value.

Hunter's increased playing time and production is due in part to the absence of Keegan Murray (ankle), who will be out for at least the next week. Hunter is still a worthy option in category leagues, but he's better in points formats.

Anfernee Simons, Philadelphia 76ers (19 percent rostered)

Don't look now, but Simons is a second-round option over the last week. Across his last three games, the sharpshooter has averaged 20 points, 1.3 steals and 5.3 triples across 27.7 minutes.

Simons is best deployed as a points-league guy, but fantasy managers can't ignore a player splashing triples and piling up points and swipes at this level.

Scoot Henderson, Portland Trail Blazers (14 percent rostered)

Ja Morant is out for at least four weeks with a hamstring injury, and in Morant's first missed game, Henderson got the start over Jrue Holiday.

Henderson posted a 14/3/1 line with three steals and a triple. The production was solid, but Henderson's playing time was most notable, as he tied Toumani Camara for team lead in minutes at 31.

Henderson appears to have the inside track to holding down Morant's vacated backcourt spot in the starting five, making him a strong add off of the waiver wire.

Moritz Wagner, Brooklyn Nets (11 percent rostered)

After spending the last five and a half seasons with Orlando, Wagner is off to a great start in his first with the Nets.

The big man averaged 15.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 triples and 1.3 "stocks" across 22 minutes in his last three games, ranking just inside the fifth round in fantasy value. Wagner won't post Top-60 value all season, but he can be a useful source of points and boards with 3-and-D upside.

Tristan da Silva, Orlando Magic (22 percent rostered)

Anthony Black was my top pickup in last week's column, but his roster percentage spiked, making him ineligible to appear again. Instead, I'll highlight da Silva, who's playing an integral role for Orlando and is still available in nearly 80% of Yahoo! leagues.

The Brazilian forward had back-to-back strong games before posting a stinker in a win over the Raptors with eight points and no peripherals. He bounced back with a 23/10/2 line, including five triples, in Sunday's loss to Boston. Until Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs are back, da Silva should continue seeing meaningful run, making him a solid add in 12-team formats.

articles.title: Toto Wolff explains George Russell's media absence after Mexican GP disappointment
articles.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff defended George Russell's decision to skip media duties after a disappointing Mexican Grand Prix
articles.body:
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal and CEO Toto Wolff described the Mexican Grand Prix as a "catastrophic moment" for George Russell .

The Briton started second on the grid after qualifying just 0.009 seconds behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton , but immediately lost ground. He was then also given a 10-second penalty for a first-lap collision with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar .

Russell ultimately finished sixth while Red Bull's Max Verstappen won. The Dutchman was joined on the podium by Hamilton and Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli. The third-place finish was enough to crown the Italian 2026 world champion. Russell congratulated his team-mate but subsequently missed his post-race media duties, resulting in a €5000 for Mercedes.

Asked whether that had been Russell's decision or the team's, Wolff told the media: "I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he's distraught about the situation. It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi.

"I have known George for such a long time, and I know for a sportsperson, this is ... He's going through a hard time, but he was also responsible for getting the young man into this team.

"So I saw him, and for a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment. Maybe today the race was a little bit of a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win."

Wolff added that the team 'let Russell down' with the energy delivery issues at the race start.

"We had the pace in the car and we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we thought it should be," the team chief continued.

"I'm very much with him at the moment. I've been in situations where it's very difficult to cope. Him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me. That's absolutely honourable."

Russell is still in the fight for second in the championship. After finishing sixth in Mexico, he dropped from second to fourth in the standings. There are currently 16 points separating second and fifth.

articles.title: 3 things we learned from Patriots in Week 8 win over Dolphins
articles.summary: The Patriots answered the bell after an ugly first half against the Dolphins. Here are three things we learned from the team's Week 8 win.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots got back in the win column in Week 8 with a 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins.

It was a hard-fought win in which the Patriots overcame a double-digit halftime deficit to defeat a division rival on the road. The team was down multiple starters heading into the game, but they stepped up in the second half to ruin the Dolphins' upset plans.

The win offered several important takeaways about the team's depth, offensive playmakers and growing chemistry as the 2026 season progresses.

Let's take a look at three things we learned about the Patriots in the key AFC East divisional win.

1. Patriots' defensive tackles are ready to step up

New England's defensive tackle depth proved to be dependable in the win over Miami.

Cory Durden delivered a disruptive performance, recording 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits. He consistently pressured Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis and played a major role in disrupting his flow in the game.

DaQuan Jones also contributed an assisted tackle and a pass defended, demonstrating that New England has reliable reinforcements capable of maintaining its defensive standard.

2. DeMario Douglas remains a high-quality threat with touchdown prowess

Douglas continued proving his value as a productive receiving option for the Patriots, as he finished with three catches for 76 yards and a 48-yard touchdown.

His knack for finding the end zone, including his success as a first-touchdown scorer for New England last season has carried over into 2026. More importantly, he has managed to step up with multiple playmakers sidelined with injuries. Wide receivers A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs missed Sunday's game against the Dolphins. And tight end Hunter Henry left the game early with a foot injury.

Douglas has maintained his level of production from last season and remains a reliable, go-to target for Maye in tough situations.

3. The Patriots' early-season woes appear to be history

After opening the season at 1-2, New England has won four of its last five games, with a tough loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 7 representing the team's only blemish in that span. The Patriots increasingly look like a cohesive unit and have displayed improved resilience, confidence and chemistry in the last five weeks.

The win over Miami provided another indication that the team is past its early-season struggles and has momentum on its side for the middle portion of the year.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Commanders: Studs and duds from Philadelphia's 27-10 loss
articles.summary: We're examining the Eagles studs and duds from their 27-10 loss to the Commanders on Sunday night
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles suffered their sixth consecutive defeat Sunday night, falling 27-10 to the Washington Commanders after an encouraging start turned into another disappointing offensive performance.

Philadelphia scored 10 points in the first quarter but couldn't add another, finishing with 268 total yards and committing two turnovers. Encouraging individual performances, particularly from several young players, were overshadowed by the Eagles ' inability to sustain drives.

Here are the studs and duds from Philadelphia's Week 8 loss.

Mukuba delivered one of Philadelphia's biggest defensive plays when he forced a first-quarter fumble by Chig Okonkwo, setting up Saquon Barkley's touchdown. The second-year safety also finished with nine tackles and a pass breakup, staying active near the football.

His performance was particularly encouraging after an early injury scare, when an interception was negated by Jonathan Greenard's offside penalty. Mukuba briefly left for evaluation but returned to contribute to the defense.

The rookie wide receiver continued to establish himself as a dependable target, leading Philadelphia with six receptions for 57 yards on nine targets. Lemon provided several of the offense's better moments and was one of the few players consistently producing through the passing game.

His growing involvement represents an important development for a team searching for offensive answers. Philadelphia needs more explosive production, but Lemon continues to show he can handle an expanded role.

Trotter made the most of his opportunity with Jihaad Campbell sidelined by injury, recording a team-high 10 tackles, including six solo stops. The second-year linebacker was frequently involved around the line of scrimmage and demonstrated the instincts that made him a productive player at Clemson.

Philadelphia still struggled against the run, but Trotter's individual performance gave the coaching staff another encouraging development to evaluate.

Philadelphia allowed five sacks and eight quarterback hits while generating just 91 rushing yards on 29 attempts. Washington frequently disrupted passing plays and prevented the Eagles from establishing any consistent rushing attack.

The offensive line's problems were particularly damaging in key situations. A strip-sack ended a promising third-quarter drive, while an illegal formation penalty on Jordan Mailata wiped out a successful field goal in the fourth quarter.

McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards, but he failed to produce a touchdown and committed two turnovers. The Eagles struggled to move the ball for long stretches, and the quarterback couldn't overcome pressure and negative plays.

The mistakes were not entirely his responsibility, but a starting quarterback must protect the football and capitalize on opportunities. McKee's interception and lost fumble made an already difficult night significantly worse.

Barkley managed just 30 yards on 13 carries, while Elijah Mitchell added 34 yards on 11 attempts. Philadelphia averaged just 3.1 yards per rushing attempt and couldn't consistently gain yards on early downs. The inability to establish the run created predictable passing situations and contributed to the offense's third-down struggles. Until Philadelphia develops a more reliable rushing attack, its offensive problems are unlikely to disappear.

articles.title: Yankees could lose two regulars as free agency unfolds
articles.summary: The Yankees could face a two-position problem this winter if Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham both leave in free […]
articles.body:
The Yankees could face a two-position problem this winter if Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham both leave in free agency. ESPN's Jorge Castillo has already outlined why that outcome is possible, and the resulting roster decisions would extend well beyond replacing two names in the lineup.

Sleeper MLB shared the outlook on Monday, attributing it to Castillo. In an October 8 offseason assessment for ESPN , Castillo wrote that the two were likely to land multiyear deals elsewhere, with his Chisholm projection conditional on a qualifying offer and the player's response.

That was a projection, not confirmation of either player's destination. Both are free agents, and a return to New York remains possible until a deal says otherwise.

The Yankees would lose different kinds of production

Chisholm hit .231/.312/.399 with 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases in 2026. His power dropped from 31 homers the previous year, but his speed still gave the lineup an element that is difficult to replace by simply finding another second baseman.

Grisham finished at .211/.308/.395 with 18 homers, down from 34 in 2025. His center-field experience matters, too, even if New York decides the cost of a multiyear deal is too high.

Together, the pair accounted for 37 regular-season home runs this year. The Yankees should not assume they can replace that power and Chisholm's speed with one internal promotion.

Castillo identified Anthony Volpe and Jose Caballero as possible options at second base, with Spencer Jones a potential answer in center field. Those are reasonable starting points, not guarantees. Using a young player in center could solve one problem while creating a new evaluation of his defense and everyday workload.

My preference is to prioritize a reliable center-field plan first, then hold an open competition at second base while keeping an external addition on the table. That gives New York a way to protect the outfield without treating a competition as a proven replacement for Chisholm's production.

The alternative is to re-sign one of the incumbents and spend the remaining resources elsewhere. Until the asking prices and the Yankees' other moves become clear, neither path is automatic. What matters is evaluating the two decisions together rather than leaving both positions to untested assumptions.

articles.title: Florida falls out of USA TODAY Sports re-rank top 25 after Georgia loss
articles.summary: Florida football's Week 9 loss to the Georgia Bulldogs has the Gators tumbling out of USA TODAY Sports' re-rank top 25.
articles.body:
The Florida Gators ended the month of October with their third loss of the 2026 campaign — an embarrassing 27-8 defeat at the hands of the Georgia Bulldogs, marking the sixth-straight loss to their cross-border rivals. Jon Sumrall's squad has no one to blame but themselves in a game plagued by boneheaded mistakes.

Following Week 9's college football schedule, USA TODAY Sports writer Paul Myerberg released his latest re-ranking of all 138 FBS teams . In it, Florida fell 11 spots to No. 33 and now sits between No. 32 SMU and No. 34 James Madison.

Compare that with the US LBM Coaches Poll, which dropped the Gators from the top 25 to the de facto No. 27 spot, and the AP Top 25 , which has them teetering on the edge at No. 25.

The SEC now has eight schools in the USA TODAY Sports re-rank top 25 this week after Florida dropped out, headlined by second-ranked Georgia, along with Kentucky (No. 8) and Texas (No. 9) among the top 10. Ole Miss (No. 11), Tennessee (No. 12), Alabama (No. 13), LSU (No. 14) and Missouri (No. 19) round out the rest of the top-ranked teams, while South Carolina sits just outside the group at No. 26.

Next up, Florida returns home to host Oklahoma on Saturday, Nov. 7, inside Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. The game is scheduled to kick off at 7:45 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on the SEC Network.

articles.title: Beat Luke Littler: Fallon Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' in Netflix show but you can't blame 'Queen of the Palace'
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' for Netflix show 'Beat Luke Littler' according to Sky Sports pundit Mark Webster; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
But this was not Sherrock's first foray into the limelight as she created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round in December 2019, and she went on to break several other barriers in the game, including becoming the first woman to reach the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts.

The 32-year-old, who was presented to the crowd in Manchester as being a hairdresser from Milton Keyes, had made more darting history in 2023 when she became the first female to produce a televised nine-dart finish.

But her inclusion in the line-up for the TV show, attracted criticism given her stature in the game, even if she met the criteria for applicants because she does not hold a PDC Tour Card.

"The backlash Fallon got is nothing she's done wrong," Webster told Sky Sports . "Ultimately, I don't think she should have been selected to play, but then you can't blame Fallon for going to try and win half a million pounds in fair play.

"It was a good leg. But look, I don't think the backlash will bother her.

"She's got a few quid, hasn't she? So she'll just crack on. People forget about these things. She just needs to get herself ready for the rest of the year now.

"She'll be quite chilled. I'm not saying she has financial burdens, but that's going to really help going forward - doing things for her."

Darts prodigy Jayden Walker, 14, who has been labelled the next Littler by fans and has taken a leg off 'The Nuke' at an exhibition event, did get a shot over one leg, but lost, while WDF No 1 Mitchell Lawrie, 15, failed to get his chance despite all the pre-event hype .

Webster thinks the format of the show was unfair, saying: "I don't think she should have been able to play. I didn't like the way it was made as an amateur beats Luke Littler, and a lot of them weren't amateurs. Fallon's a professional player.

"I think Mitchell Lawrie was due to play as well, but he didn't get on. I do think they should have played out the remaining legs and then they could have chipped away at Fallon's money if they'd won. So one more win, they split Fallon's money, just for a bit of jeopardy.

"I thought it was a brilliant show. The production was fantastic.

"The concept of it was good. I just think the selection process is kind of a bit of a grey area."

Hearn: Sherrock is not a PDC Tour Card holder

PDC chief Barry Hearn, who was involved in the audition process, defended the line-up.

Asked whether Sherrock's inclusion was unfair, he said: "No, not at all. She's not a PDC Tour Card holder. She's entitled to enter. Why should she be denied?

"She's a well-known player and she's a very good player. But Mitchell Lawrie is a very well-known player and an excellent player.

"Do you want just a series of 20 matches where someone can't even throw a dart? No, of course we want excellence competing against excellence, and that's what it was all about."

articles.title: 2028 DB commit says he's sticking with FSU despite coaching change
articles.summary: 2028 three-star defensive back Man Robinson pledges his loyalty to Florida State after the firing of Mike Norvell.
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles are heading into an entirely new era with their football program. Head coach Mike Norvell was fired on Sunday along with multiple position coaches. This was a move that simply had to be made.

The focus now shifts to not only finding a new coach but keeping recruiting classes together. FSU currently has the No. 6 class in the 2028 cycle. The top-ranked player that's committed is three-star cornerback Man Robinson, who is being recruited as a safety.

Changing coaches calls into question if recruits who are committed will stick around. Robinson took to social media on Sunday night to express how he felt. He announced that he's staying in Tallahassee.

The 247Sports composite rankings have Robinson listed as the No. 430 prospect in the nation and the No. 43 cornerback. He's also the No. 51 recruit in the state of 51.

Florida State also parted ways with safeties coach Evan Cooper on Sunday, and he had a hand in getting Robinson to commit. So, much like 2028 three-star athlete Chayse Brown saying that he's staying with FSU, Robinson's statement is big.

articles.title: Nikita Kucherov Explains Lightning Trade Request in Video Amid NHL Rumors on Contract Talks
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov explained his shocking trade request from the team.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov explained his shocking trade request from the team.

The two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner cited "poor communication" and a lack of respect from the organization. He told reporters his had limited contact of late with general manager Julien BriseBois, as one example, with his free agency looming on the horizon:

Kucherov has spent his entire career in Tampa Bay. He's second all time in goals (405) and first in assists (737) and points (1,142).

The 33-year-old remains an elite forward as well. He finished 2025-26 with 44 goals and 86 assists, and only the Edmonton Oilers' Connor McDavid had more points.

Needless to say, news of Kucherov's request sent shockwaves across the league.

ESPN's Emily Kaplan reported last week his contract situation played a pivotal role: "Negotiations between Tampa Bay and Kucherov's camp remained far apart, sources said, and that gulf led to a meeting Friday in which Kucherov said he would not be re-signing this summer and wanted to play elsewhere."

Kucherov's media availability Monday shed more light on the situation. Whatever the exact specifics, there's clearly a massive divide between the player and team.

BriseBois issued a statement last Friday to say the Lightning "unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita."

Ahead of a 5-4 loss to the Nashville Predators, coach Jon Cooper told reporters there are no questions as to Kucherov's effort level or commitment, either.

"I will sit here and tell you nothing has changed in what our goals are this year just, maybe, the context of how it is going to go about," he said. "Kuch is 100 percent a part of this team. He wants to be a part of this team for this season and he is committed to be with the group that loves him and the group he loves.

"What I don't want to get skewed in all of this is if Kuch turns the puck over or the play does not go exactly his way and he shows frustration or, at some point, the coach who is coaching him is showing frustration with him or somebody else on the team and, then, everybody says, 'Oh my God. He wants out.' That will not be the case."

Kucherov could escalate things and refuse to suit up for Tampa Bay, which is the route Dylan Larkin has taken with the Detroit Red Wings. In general, a lot can change between now and the March 1, 2027, trade deadline.

As long as he's willing to play, the Lightning are bound to dig in their heels and rebuff any trade offers.

articles.title: WWE Royal Rumble 2027 Date, Location Announced for Start of Road to WrestleMania 43
articles.summary: The road to WrestleMania 43 will officially begin in the desert.
articles.body:
The road to WrestleMania 43 will officially begin in the desert.

WWE announced on Monday that the 2027 Royal Rumble will take place on Feb. 6 at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. This will mark the 40th edition of the fan-favorite event.

Feb. 6 is the latest Royal Rumble date WWE has ever scheduled, and this will be just the second time in the event's history that it is held in February. This will be Arizona's third time hosting the event, following previous editions in 2013 and 2019.

The Royal Rumble is regarded as the start of the road to WrestleMania because the male and female winners of the namesake matches go on to earn world title shots at the marquee event in April. Last year, Roman Reigns and Liv Morgan were victorious at the Royal Rumble in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and went on to win the World Heavyweight Championship and the Women's World Championship, respectively, at WrestleMania 42.

In addition to the Royal Rumble, WWE announced that Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale will host a double event on Friday, Feb. 5, featuring both Friday Night SmackDown and AAA Road to Rey de Reyes.

The Royal Rumble can be a star-making showcase for rising young Superstars like Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Lash Legend and Lola Vice, so fans will be excited to see who emerges from the fray when things go down on Feb. 6.

articles.title: Kirby Smart clarifies comments after taking shot at how much college football players are making
articles.summary: Kirby Smart suggested Georgia Bulldogs players may lack the hunger of past championship teams now that NIL money rivals what he earned until 40.
articles.body: Several years into the name, image, and likeness era, college football fans are now familiar with most of the resulting changes happening across the sport. Parity within the major conferences is rapidly increasing, with the gaps between teams dropping dramatically. Players who used to commit to sit on the bench at Alabama under Nick Saban or Ohio State under Ryan Day are now bringing in bigger paydays to start at smaller schools. For good reason. The combination of NIL and the transfer portal has made rebuilding a program overnight more realistic than it's ever been. Curt Cignetti turned the Indiana Hoosiers from an also-ran into an undefeated, National Championship-winning behemoth in just two seasons. Bob Chesney came to UCLA from James Madison and overnight, made the Bruins into a legitimate College Football Playoff contender, sitting at No. 5 in the latest Associated Press Top 25 poll late into the season. THE CIGNETTI EFFECT IS REAL: INDIANA FOOTBALL SPARKS AN UNBELIEVABLE 'REVIVAL' IN BLOOMINGTON But Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart may have tacitly admitted to another result from the NIL era: a lack of motivation and aggression for the week-in, week-out grind of major conference college football. After the Bulldogs easily handled the Florida Gators 27-8, Smart was asked about the number of injuries his team is dealing with, and whether playing a tough SEC schedule could contribute to it. And his answer was revealing about the state of modern college football, particularly with the amount of money that's now floating around it. "Everybody is practicing less, but everybody’s getting injured more," he said. "I think about the teams we had in ’21 and ’22, and how physical they were and how they practiced. We can’t even get close to that now," Smart added. "If it’s a different culture that guys don’t want to as much, I don’t know. They were definitely hungrier, because there was a motivation to make it. A lot of these guys, honestly, they make more than I did until I was 40. It’s just a different day and age." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER It's an important insight that may have been obvious, but is frequently unsaid. Players may not feel the need to improve as much as they used to, because they're not fighting for the NFL payday down the road, they're already making significant money. It's human nature, and likely true, but it's one of the perhaps unexpected ancillary outcomes of players now being able to earn money for their contributions. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Still, Smart's comments received some blowback, with some adding that Smart's doing pretty well financially, and that coaches have frequently displayed a financially-motivated lack of loyalty or commitment to stick with their teams. If they can benefit from the money being generated by college football, why shouldn't the players putting themselves on the line benefit as well? Unsurprisingly, he clarified those comments on Monday, saying he thinks it's "awesome" that young athletes are able to earn money in college sports now. "I think it’s awesome that players are getting paid. I wish they were being paid when I played because then maybe I wouldn’t have had to get a $5,000 job for the summer trying to work. But that is none of my concern. It is more long-term effect of earning power, what is the value of a dollar, do I actually know how hard it is to go out in the real world, and gotta go work for $60,000? That outlook can be tough on guys. But the earning power they have while they’re here, more power to them." Again, it's an obvious fact that 18-year-olds now able to make that much money, or far, far, more is going to have some other side effects. Motivation being one of them. But like all jobs and careers, if they fail to live up to expectations, because of a lack of motivation, it can all change in the blink of an eye. Smart added that it's now even more important to evaluate how a player will respond to making that kind of money, and whether it'll impact their ability to contribute moving forward. "That still is an art in recruiting and decision-making: Are you recruiting the right kinds of kids that will not be affected by that," Smart said. "We used to deal with that all the time when I was at Alabama, when you’d have an (NFL) scout come in and say, ‘Well, is him being a first-round pick or second-round pick going to change him?’ That’s your job to decide that, not mine. "Well, now it’s our job to decide as coaches. Do you have the right kind of people in your program who will be motivated for the team, and the culture of the program?" When the 2025 House settlement limited rosters to 105 players instead of effectively unlimited, coaches were less willing to go all out in practice and risk injuries. That, Smart believes, is part of the change to college football. Maybe it's both. Maybe it's none of it, and it's just random variance. It's hard to know, in the modern era, with how many changes there are seemingly week-to-week. Given the chaos this season has brought already, at least the increase in parity has made for more exciting television.

The WWE champion blasted Reigns, reminding him and the fans that they will remember his match with the Jackass star for the next decade, while no one remembers anything about the world champion's "sixth-of-12" match against Brock Lesnar.

A fired-up Reigns expressed disdain for what Zayn has become and, more importantly, that he ruined what he spent time creating. He vowed to win Saturday and demanded that Brooklyn acknowledge him to close things out.

This was an extraordinary promo. Zayn was otherworldly and his line about being the "g*****n WWE Champion" would have been the perfect exclamation point in any other situation. Reigns was equally great, remaining confident while clearly shaken by Zayn's criticisms. Their match Saturday might be an all-timer in the making.

It is still amazing how over Reigns remains as a when at its core, this OTC character is no different than the heel character that reigned supreme for four years.

Reigns claimed that had he not beaten Brock Lesnar for the WWE title at WrestleMania 38, Zayn wouldn't hold it today because it would not exist, is wrong. The only title that would not exist today is the world title that he currently holds.

articles.title: Fractured tibia for Kendrick Bourne
articles.summary: Cardinals WR Kendrick Bourne will not need surgery for injury but will miss rest of season
articles.body:
Updating a previous report, Arizona Cardinals WR Kendrick Bourne (leg) has been diagnosed with a fractured tibia and will be sidelined for three months, according to a source. He will not need to undergo surgery to repair the injury.

Why It Matters: Bourne will likely be placed on the Reserve/Injured list in the near future and will miss the rest of the season. Michael Wilson and Trey McBride are the only Cardinals pass catchers that should be weekly starting options in fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Giants Hold NFC East Lead As Eagles Stumble To 2-6 Record
articles.summary: The Giants sit alone in first place while the Eagles slump. Big Blue View breaks down the standings after Dallas and Washington's weekend results.
articles.body:
The New York Giants own the NFC East right now, and the gap is getting wider. Week 9 finds the team firmly leading the division, according to Ed Valentine of Big Blue View. The record stands at 4-2-1, a mark that puts them ahead of every other team in their own group. This lead did not come from a perfect week, but from the failures of their rivals while the Giants sat out.

While New York rested, Dallas blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead against the Arizona Cardinals, according to Big Blue View . The Cowboys ended up losing 33-30 in overtime, missing a huge chance to close the gap. Washington also got the better of the other division foe, beating the Philadelphia Eagles 27-10. The Commanders improved to 2-5-1, but the real story is the Eagles falling to 2-6. While the Giants rested during their bye week, Big Blue View observed that Sunday's division outcomes favored them.

The standings show a clear hierarchy that favors the home team in the NFC. The Giants sit at 4-2-1 with a 1-0-1 record in the NFC East. Dallas drops to 3-5, while Washington sits at 2-5-1. The Eagles have fallen to 2-6 with a 1-2 NFC record. These numbers tell a simple story: the Giants are the only team in the division with a winning record. The rest of the group is trying to catch up from behind.

Per Big Blue View, the weekend was good to the Giants because their competition dropped points. The 3-5 Cowboys missed an opportunity to gain ground on the Giants on Sunday. That loss in Arizona leaves Dallas three games back in the loss column. The Commanders and Eagles are even further behind, making the path to the playoffs look much clearer for New York.

The Giants will test this lead on the road next. The schedule has the team heading to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff. They face an Eagles squad that has lost four of its last five games and sits at the bottom of the division. A win in Philadelphia would push the Giants to 5-2-1 and make the gap nearly impossible to bridge for the other three teams.

After that trip to Philly, the team returns home for a Thursday night game against the Commanders. The schedule is tough, but the position is strong. If the Giants can split these two games, they will be in the driver's seat for the rest of the season.

Big Blue View listed the NFC playoff standings with the Giants holding the third seed. The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings lead the conference at 6-1, but the Giants are the top team in their division. The Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, and Philadelphia Eagles all trail the Giants in the loss column. The NFC East race is far from over, but the Giants have built a cushion that no other team in the division can match right now.

articles.title: Lighthouse Christian falls in NACA championship game
articles.summary: DAYTON, Tenn. — Lighthouse Christian ended its inaugural season with a 5-0 loss in the National Association of Christian Athletes tournament championship to...
articles.body:
DAYTON, Tenn. — Lighthouse Christian ended its inaugural season with a 5-0 loss in the National Association of Christian Athletes tournament championship to Gateway Legacy Christian Friday.

Gateway led 3-0 at halftime and added two more in the second half. Jouquliam Pereira led Gateway with two goals, while Jose Neto, Pedro Chierirato and Lotenzo Peria also scored.

The Seahawks end the season with a 23-5-1 record.

Three Lighthouse senior starters played in their final game for the Seahawks: Sammy Scritchfield, Elijah Ziler and Peyton Poland.

Poland made 25 saves on Friday, ending with 527 for his career.

Gateway Legacy is based in Florissant, Missouri, which is outside of St. Louis.

"They accepted the challenge, played with courage, passion, and grit, and never backed down," Lighthouse Christian coach David Ziler said. "They never quit and represented Lighthouse Christian Academy with tremendous character."

XENIA, Ohio — Bishop Walsh lost two games to end its season at the National Christian School Athletic Association tournament Thursday and Friday.

The Spartans fell to New York's Chautauqua Christian 3-1 in the Division 5 semifinals Thursday before losing to Virginia's Mountain Mission 3-0 in Friday's third-place game.

Bishop Walsh ends the season at 4-1-7-1.

articles.title: Tigers re-up with veteran right-handers Drew Anderson, Jacob Waguespack
articles.summary: The Tigers pick up the $10 million team option on Drew Anderson and sign reliever Jacob Waguespack to a one-year, $1.3 million major league contract.
articles.body:
DETROIT – The Tigers, as expected, picked up the $10 million team option on right-hander Drew Anderson for 2027 and declined a $12 million option with a $2 million buyout on reliever Kenley Jansen.

In addition, the Tigers signed reliever Jacob Waguespack to a one-year, $1.3 million major league contract for 2027.

Waguespack, who will turn 33 on Thursday, Nov. 5, can earn an additional $1.5 million in performance bonuses —$25,000 for reaching both 45 innings and 50 innings pitched; $50,000 for reaching 55 innings, 60 innings and 65 innings pitched.

Acquired in a cash deal from Milwaukee on June 10 last season, Waguespack became one of manager AJ Hinch's most trusted relievers, posting a 2.49 ERA and 0.915 WHIP covering 47 innings in 35 games.

Anderson, 32, started the season in the Tigers' bullpen but finished in the rotation, producing a 2.61 ERA and 1.2 WHIP in 11 starts. He is expected to compete for a rotation spot in 2027.

The Tigers also activated seven players off the 60-day injured list: Reliever Will Vest, starter Reese Olson, shortstop Trey Sweeney and outfielders Kerry Carpenter, Parker Meadows, Wenceel Perez and Matt Vierling.

To clear space on the 40-man roster, the Tigers removed four players: Pitchers Bailey Horn and Sawyer Gipson-Long were placed on unconditional release waivers; outfielder Corey Julks was outrighted and is now a free agent; pitcher Yilber Dias was designated for assignment.

The Tigers' 40-man roster stands at 40 players.

articles.title: NKU opens season with win in Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon
articles.summary: UTEP knocked down 14 of 24 free throws while the Norse made 30 of 33 in the Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon in Sioux Falls, S.D.
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. − The new-look UTEP basketball team had a quite familiar old problem in its opening 84-76 loss to Northern Kentucky: The Miners still lose games from the free-throw line.

Playing against a team that won 20 games last year as a member of the Horizon League, UTEP knocked down 14 of 24 free throws while the Norse made 30 of 33, wiping out a number of things UTEP did well in the Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon in Sioux Falls, S.D.

UTEP trailed most of the game, rarely by double figures, and was within 69-66 inside 4 minutes to go before a five-point NKU run proved more than the Miners could overcome. The Norse shot 50% to UTEP's 38% and the Miners made 8-of-30 3-pointers, as some other old problems of shooting arose. UTEP also struggled to contain NKU's guards, accounting for much of the 24 Miner fouls.

"We've got a starting point now," coach Joe Golding said. "There's plenty that we've got to get better at on both sides of the floor. Offensively we shoot 39% for the game, we let them shoot 50%, and then the free throw line they outscored us 16. We had 14 offensive boards and only got 10 points out of it.

"If I'm frustrated with anything, it's the toughness. We've got to get tougher on both sides of the ball. There is plenty of work work to do on the offensive and defensive ends. We have to get a lot better this week."

Freshman Willie Foster led NKU with 24 points and 10 rebounds and senior Noah Pagotto also had a double-double with 19 points and 12 rebounds.

Freshman Youssouf Traore led the Miners with 18 points and six rebounds, Donovan Criss added 13 points and Augusto Cassia had 10 points.

articles.title: Terrifying Moment: Lions’ Jack Campbell Remains Hospitalized
articles.summary: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remains hospitalized after a frightening neck injury. Teammates pray while early signs look positive.
articles.body:
Football is a violent game, but nothing prepares you for the sight of a player lying still on the turf. Jack Campbell, the Lions' All-Pro linebacker, is still in the hospital after a terrifying hit against the Vikings on Sunday. The team released an update on Monday stating that early signs are positive regarding his neck injury, yet they refused to share more details out of respect for his family.

This was not a routine play. Campbell went down face first after colliding with tight end T.J. Hockenson during the fourth quarter. He was alert and breathing when taken off the field, but the scene left the entire stadium in shock. Detroit coach Dan Campbell had no fresh news during his press conference, so he asked everyone to take a knee and pray. "We don't know anything else at this point. So here's what I wanna do. We're gonna take a knee. Now I wanna pray for Jack, and let's keep him in our thoughts and prayers, man," he said, according to the New York Post .

The emotional toll hit hard for the players who saw it happen. Quarterback Jared Goff spoke plainly about how the moment shook the team. "Jack's deal was definitely scary," he said. Goff reminded everyone that Campbell is a husband and a father, which is why the fear runs so deep. It brings you back to reality for a moment; as Goff noted, these athletes are real people with lives outside the gridiron, but if anyone is tough enough to get through something like that, it is Campbell.

Campbell is not just a body on the field; he is the heart of the Lions' defense. The team signed him to a four-year extension last May that runs through the 2030 season. He earned All-Pro honors last year after becoming the only player in the NFL with 150-plus tackles and five sacks, while also forcing three fumbles. The Lions drafted him with the 18th overall pick in 2023, and he has started 53 games since then. Losing him, even for a short time, would be a massive blow to a 5-2 team .

The medical staff moved fast to stabilize him before he was carted off to a local Detroit hospital. The team will not release further updates until they have more concrete information. Fans are left waiting, hoping that the positive signs the Lions reported on Monday lead to a full recovery.

articles.title: Watkins returns with 21 points, Hall scores 22 in debut as USC rolls past UNLV for a 100-68 victory.
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — JuJu Watkins scored 21 points in her return after missing last season with an ACL injury, freshman Saniyah Hall added 22 in her collegiate d...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — JuJu Watkins scored 21 points in her return after missing last season with an ACL injury, freshman Saniyah Hall added 22 in her collegiate debut and No. 3 Southern California defeated UNLV 100-68 on Monday.

Jazzy Davidson led all scorers with 23 points on 10-for-11 shooting for the Trojans. Hall added seven rebounds and seven assists.

Kennedy Smith contributed 12 points and Sitaya Fagan had 11 for USC, giving the Trojans five scorers in double figures. Watkins added five rebounds and two assists in 25 minutes.

Maia Rosarion led UNLV with 12 points and Jayla Constant added 10. Meadow Roland grabbed a game-high nine rebounds for the Lady Rebels, who finished with a 40-35 rebounding advantage.

Watkins scored 11 points during a decisive third quarter in which USC outscored UNLV 31-10, stretching a 52-39 halftime lead to 83-49. The Trojans made 14 of 20 shots in the period while holding the Lady Rebels to 3-for-16 shooting.

Hall scored seven points and Davidson added six in the third, with both making all three of their field-goal attempts. UNLV missed all five of its 3-point attempts and went without a field goal over the final 4:14 of the quarter.

USC shot 58.8% overall and held a 52-24 advantage in points in the paint. The Trojans forced 24 turnovers, converting them into 32 points, and recorded 13 steals.

Hall scored nine points in the first quarter as USC built a 29-15 lead. UNLV outscored the Trojans 24-23 in the second quarter, making four of six 3-pointers before USC pulled away after halftime.
